stories.title: NBA issues retroactive flagrant foul to Keldon Johnson after officials missed his blatant groin kick of Devin Booker
stories.summary: NBA officials need to do better.
stories.detailText: Keldon Johnson got away with shenanigans in real time. But the NBA’s not letting him off the hook. The NBA announced Tuesday that it’s issued a postgame flagrant foul 1 to the San Antonio Spurs guard for an infraction during Monday’s blowout win over the Phoenix Suns. The infraction? He kicked Devin Booker in the groin, very clearly so. Booker went down to the court in obvious pain. But game officials chose to move along as if nothing happened. Here’s the incriminating video that the Suns were happy to post on their social media Tuesday. Tuesday, Keldon Johnson was assessed a postgame Flagrant Foul Penalty 1 for his kick on Devin Booker in Monday's game. The play was not reviewed in real-time. pic.twitter.com/z3lxCWdjIN — PHNX Suns (@PHNX_Suns) November 10, 2026 That isn’t subtle. Referee Natalie Sago was standing with a clear view of the infraction, and nothing was called on the floor. So play ensued as Booker writhed in pain on the court until the Suns were forced to call a timeout. But there was a chance to rectify the situation from there. Per the NBA rulebook , coaches aren’t permitted to challenge a non-call. Suns coach Jordan Ott had no recourse to initiate a replay review. But game officials do. Under the “Altercation” heading in the NBA rulebook , officials may initiate a replay review absent a foul called on the floor when: A player, coach, trainer or other bench person commits a hostile act against another player, referee, coach, trainer, bench person or spectator This is generally applied when there’s a two-way altercation. If Booker had kicked Johnson in the groin in response, they would have almost certainly gone to the tape to issue Johnson his deserved flagrant foul that really warranted flagrant 2 with an ejection. But the language clearly gives officials leeway to go to the monitor when a player “commits a hostile act against another player.” A groin kick is the definition of a hostile act. NBA referees are more than happy to stop play to go to the monitor for lesser infractions. The only solace here is that the game was a blowout. The Spurs held a 15-point lead at the time in a game that they won, 122-96. A properly called flagrant foul wasn’t likely to shift the outcome of the game. But that’s likely of little comfort to Booker. Game officials need to do better.

stories.title: Warriors lose guard Brandon Williams to mild hamstring strain
stories.summary: The Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's win, sources told ESPN.
stories.detailText: The Golden State Warriors will be without reserve guard Brandon Williams for at least a week after he strained his left hamstring during Monday night's 138-87 win over the New Orleans Pelicans , the team announced Tuesday. Williams entered late in the first quarter, burst to the rim for two quick layups but came up hobbled on the second and limped to the locker room after only 99 seconds of action. The Warriors soon announced that Williams was out with a hamstring issue and scheduled for an MRI. Those results revealed the mild strain, ruling him out for the Warriors' difficult upcoming road trip to Houston, San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis. Williams has been an immediate bench spark in his first season with the Warriors, averaging 10.4 points and 2.3 assists in only 16.4 minutes per game, providing scoring punch the moment Stephen Curry rests. Williams has 17 and 20 points in the two games that Curry missed this season, including a win over the LA Clippers as part of the Warriors' current eight-game win streak. But left hamstring issues have followed Williams early in his NBA career. He strained it in the 2025 preseason while with Dallas and subsequently missed time last March while dealing with tightness. The Warriors, while surging at 8-3, are significantly depleted. Starting wings Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are rehabbing serious knee injuries, projected starting center Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away from basketball entirely and they lost backup guard Will Richard to a UCL tear in his left thumb over the weekend. Richard has been upgraded to questionable for the Warriors' game in Houston on Wednesday night. He has explored the feasibility of wearing a splint on his left thumb and playing through the injury. Gary Payton II is out with left knee inflammation.

stories.title: Futures Basketball League to launch in April for U18 players
stories.summary: The Futures Basketball League announced plans Tuesday to launch in April 2027, targeting the top 120 under-18 players in the country.
stories.detailText: A new league backed by investments from LeBron James and Kevin Durant is aiming to reshape top-level youth basketball. The Futures League announced plans Tuesday to launch in April 2027, targeting the top 120 under-18 players in the country with hopes to replace a patchwork of summer league tournaments and travel leagues, many run by shoe companies. "The top 150 basketball players under 18 in the country play on over 200 different teams in seven different leagues in the spring and summer season," said Jason Stein, the league's chairman and co-founder. "And it's not fair they don't get fair value for their NIL and they don't get professional coaching structure -- so this needs to exist." Stein said players will be paid through NIL deals and maintain their eligibility for college and high school. The start-up hopes to combine the television appeal of the Little League World Series, the in-person excitement once enjoyed by the And1 Live Tour and the emphasis on player development of European youth sports academies. Combined, Stein said, the Futures League is attempting to build something that is both commercially successful and helps the much-maligned youth basketball development pipeline in the United States. Currently, travel league circuits sponsored by different shoe companies don't play each other, meaning the best players aren't always competing against each other. Many of those players don't receive NIL deals for their participation. Then there are the concerns about too many games and travel leagues that emphasize individual performance over team-building skills. "It's something that I wish that I would have had when I was playing when I was a youngster," said former NBA star Derrick Rose, an investor in the league who will also run its Chicago team. The league plans to launch a season next year that runs from April through August, culminating in a championship. It will begin with 12 teams, each representing a geographic region. Teams will recruit players within that territory, but players will be contracted and paid by the league. The league said the price to buy into a team has been $6 million, and investors also get equity in the league. Stein intends to sell sponsorships and secure a media rights deal to broadcast games. Investors include LRMR, a fund started by James and his business partner Maverick Carter; Boardroom Sports Holdings, a fund launched by Durant and his business partner Rich Kleinman; and team owners Paolo Banchero (a forward on the Orlando Magic ), Rose and investor Gary Vaynerchuk. The league declined to say how much it would pay players for NIL deals; Rose said the amounts could be "life changing." The league will also help facilitate NIL deals for players with additional sponsors. Players can choose to receive their pay in cash, league equity or a combination of both, according to a statement from the league Tuesday. Tom Farrey, executive director of the Aspen Institute's Sports & Society Program, said today's youth basketball system isn't adequately developing players. "It's commercializing and monetizing them at every stage without any adherence to athletic or child development principles," he said. Stein said those effects are felt in the NBA today: "There's a lack of professional coaching and structure [in youth basketball], and there hasn't been an American-born MVP in the NBA since 2018. Can you imagine if the Ballon d'Or had gone to an American-born soccer player for the last eight years? There would be riots in the streets of Europe." Rose told ESPN he is currently meeting with representatives from Northern Trust to build out a financial literacy program for his team, another draw of the league that will help prepare players for a professional career. Rose said he'll soon begin recruiting. "Voltaire said you judge a man by his questions," he said of his recruiting pitch. "I'm just gonna ask some simple questions about what they did prior to me actually coming to them and what I could do to help them going forward. I want them to just understand the business of basketball, because now it's really a business, so it's me opening myself up to them." One question for the Futures League is how it will recruit players away from the current summer league circuits, while also not alienating the major shoe companies. "It's great they want to pay the kids, but the question is always what the sneaker companies are going to do," said Sonny Vaccaro, the former sneaker promoter and amateurism critic, who ran a successful high school basketball camp for decades. Stein said he has had productive conversations with those companies and plans to work with them. This is not the first attempt to monetize or improve youth basketball development, but there have been fits and starts that speak to the opportunity and the challenge - as well as the competition. Overtime Sports created a paid league for top teenagers , first requiring them to forfeit high school and college eligibility only to amend those rules. The NBA launched a Jr. NBA league that secured a broadcast rights deal in the mold of the Little League World Series but aired for only two years. The NBA also was touting as recently as last year a program called Court of Leaders, which sought to mentor top young players about professionalism and leadership before they got to the league but since scrapped it and laid off multiple members of its youth basketball development division, according to multiple people familiar with the matter. (A league spokesman said: "The NBA is committed to expanding access to youth basketball and supporting the next generation of elite players in the U.S. and around the world." They added that James Jones, the former NBA player, is the new leader of Elite Player Strategy and Damien Wilkins, another former player, was hired to lead the department domestically.) Stein co-founded SC, a holding company with investments across sports and entertainment, including a major stake in the United Pickleball Association that has grown substantially, he said. "We've outgrown the old system," Stein said. "First college [got NIL] and now it's inevitable that the next level of talent, guys who have tens of thousands, if not hundreds of thousands of Instagram followers, and they're doing brand deals, and they're a year away from a $5 million contract from Duke. It can't be zero-to-that anymore."

stories.title: Boston Celtics (8-2) at Philadelphia 76ers (9-2) Game #11 11/10/26
stories.summary: The Celtics visit the Philadelphia for the 1st of 4 games between them this season.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 16: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Philadelphia 76ers dribbles the ball during the game against the Boston Celtics on October 16, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Boston Celtics (8-2) at Philadelphia 76ers (9-2) Tuesday, November 10, 2026 8:00 PM ET Game #11 Road #6 TV: Peacock/NBC Radio: 98.5 The Sports Hub, 97.5 The Fanatic, Sirius XM Xfinity Mobile Arena The Celtics visit the Philadelphia 76ers for the first of 4 games between them this season. They will meet in Philadelphia again on February 7. They will meet twice in Boston on January 21 and March 7. This is likely the most anticipated matchup of the season so far as there are many stories to watch in this game. First, there is the beef, or the lamb chops and gravy, or whatever you want to call what has been going on between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown since the trade. In the preseason, as they were both warming up, they didn’t even acknowledge each other. There has been a back and forth of words between them ever since. Also there is the story of Paul George returning to Philly for the first time and of Jaylen Brown and PG13 facing their former teams. There is also the story of the long time rivalry between the Celtics and 76ers and the teams who faced each other in the 2nd round of the playoffs last season. There is also the story of the top 2 teams in the East facing off. The 8-2 Celtics are 2nd in the East with only Philadelphia (9-2) half a game ahead of them in the standings. The Celtics have won their last 3 games and the 76ers are looking for their 2nd straight win. The Celtics are 2-2 on the road while the 76ers are 4-2 at home. The Celtics won both games in the preseason. Both teams are 2-0 in games against division rivals. The Celtics are playing in the first of back to back games. This is their 3rd back to back set this season already. They won the first game in both of their back to back sets this season. One win was at home while the other was on the road. The Celtics are 275-200 overall all time against the 76ers. They are 94-130 in games played in Philly. They tied the series 2-2 last season, with each team winning one at home and one on the road. The 76ers made one of the biggest moves of the off season, trading Paul George to the Celtics to get Jaylen Brown. They also signed LeBron James, Dean Wade, Ariel Hukporti and Anfernee Simons as free agents. They drafted Labaron Philon, Jr with the 22nd pick in the draft. Along with Paul George, they lost Quentin Grimes, Kelly Oubre, Jr and Andre Drummond. Mike Gansey also replaced Daryl Morey as the 76ers’ president of basketball operations. After this game, the Celtics will complete their 4 game road trip with a game in Toronto in back to back games Wednesday. Then they play Dallas and Orlando at home before a West coast trip that takes them through Denver, Sacramento, Golden State, and Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it’s home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. The 76ers will host Toronto and Indiana before road games at Brooklyn and Orlando. Then they host Milwaukee, Portland and Miami before games at Indiana and Houston. Then they have a 3 game home stand against Memphis, Denver and Orlando before playing at Orlando. Next they host Dallas and play at Charlotte. They will host Houston before a 5 game Western road trip. The Celtics have been changing their starting lineup with Jordan Walsh, Hugo Gonzalez, Baylor Scheierman, and Neemias Queta getting starts along with Derrick White, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Mitchell Robinson. The starting lineup is a work in progress for the Celtics, especially the shooting guard spot that has changed pretty much from game to game. Mike Conley got the start against the Bucks, but I’m guessing that White, Walsh, George, Tatum and Queta get the start in this one. The 76ers should start Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, James and Embiid. The Celtics have no one on the injury report as of this time. Chris Cenac, Jr and the Celtics 3 two way players will likely be with Maine. The 76ers have 3 players out as of now. Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow are both out due to back injuries. Ariel Hukporti is out for the season due to a torn Achilles. Joel Embiid has been struggling with plantar faciitis but is expected to play in this game. Probable Starting Matchups PG: Derrick White vs Tyrese Maxey Derrick White | Getty Images Tyrese Maxey | Getty Images SG: Jordan Walsh vs VJ Edgecombe Jordan Walsh | NBAE via Getty Images VJ Edgecombe | Getty Images SF: Paul George vs Jaylen Brown Paul George | NBAE via Getty Images Jaylen Brown | NBAE via Getty Images PF: Jayson Tatum vs Lebron James Jayson Tatum | NBAE via Getty Images LeBron James | Getty Images C: Neemias Queta vs Joel Embiid Neemias Queta | Getty Images Joel Embiid | Getty Images Celtics Reserves Chris Cenac, Jr Mike Conley, Jr Luka Garza Jordan Walsh Ron Harper, Jr Sam Hauser Payton Pritchard Mitchell Robinson Baylor Scheierman Two Way Players Devin Carter Dillon Mitchell Amari Williams Injuries/Out None Listed Head Coach Joe Mazzulla 76ers Reserves Anfernee Simons Dean Wade Kentavious Caldwell-Pope Jabari Walker Justin Edwards Lebaron Philon, Jr, 2-Way Players Taco Fall Rayan Rupert Caleb Love Injuries/Out Adem Bona (back) out Dominick Barlow (back) out Ariel Hukporti (Achilles) out Head Coach Nick Nurse Key Matchups Derrick White vs Tyrese Maxey Maxey is averaging 26.9 points, 3.7 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.4 steals per game. He is shooting 48.1% from the field and 34.1% from beyond the arc. His 26.9 ppg ranks 3rd in the East. He is quick and so the Celtics will need to work hard to stay in front of him. They will need Derrick White’s defense to be sharp in this one. Paul George vs Jaylen Brown This should be an incredible matchup to watch. Brown is averaging 22.3 points, 6.7 rebounds, 4.0 assists, and 1.2 steals. He is shooting 47.7% from the field and 39.2% from beyond the arc. I expect Brown to come in with a chip on his shoulder to prove that he is the better player among Paul George, Jayson Tatum and himself. Paul George just needs to focus on playing team ball and being his best self. Honorable Mention Neemias Queta vs Joel Embiid Embiid is averaging 17.9 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game. He is shooting 38% from the field and 10% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to keep Embiid out of the paint and off the boards. Queta needs to find a way to stay out of foul trouble and to counter Embiid on defense. Keys to the Game Defense – As always, defense is absolutely the key to winning this, and every, game. It is very true that defense wins championships. Shots don’t always fall but players can always play hard on defense. The Celtics are 3rd with an offensive rating of 117.9 while the 76ers are 20th with an offensive rating of 110.3. The Celtics are 4th with a defensive rating of 106.3. The 76ers aren’t far behind with a defensive rating of 107.6. The Celtics must give full out effort on defense for every minute of this game if they hope to beat the loaded 76ers team. Rebound – Next to defense, rebounding is always a big key to winning. The key to rebounding is effort and focus. The 76ers are 19th with 43.4 rebounds per game while the Celtics are 10th with 45.0 rebounds per game. The Celtics have to fight as a team to try to grab every rebound to avoid the 76ers getting 2nd chance points because the 76ers average 14.7 second chance points per game. In order to win the possession battle, the Celtics must crash the boards and fight for every rebound. Effort and Focus for 48 Minutes – The Celtics have to play with extra effort overall for all 4 quarters. They have to stay focused on playing basketball the right way as a team. They have to avoid getting wound up in the Tatum vs Brown and Brown vs George narratives. They have to play team ball and give all out effort to get to the basket, to defend, to rebound, to hustle after loose balls and to play hard on every possession. Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics play the best when they move the ball and find the best shot. They struggle when they try to do too much individually. But, they have to be careful handling the ball and making passes. The 76ers are best in the league at taking care of the ball with just 12.9 turnovers per game. The Celtics are 12th with 14.9 turnovers per game. They have to stay focused and avoid turning the ball over. X-Factors On the Road – The Celtics will be on the road once again for the 3rd straight game and they will be facing a very hostile crowd. Philly fans hate the Celtics because they have pretty much owned them in recent years. They hate Jayson Tatum because the Celtics took him with Philly’s pick after the 76ers traded up to take Markelle Fultz. They now have another reason to hate the Celtics and that is to back up Jaylen Brown who has been very bitter against the Celtics and his former running mate. There will likely be a lot of boos and the Celtics need to play through them. They have to shake off the distractions of playing on the road and stay focused on playing Celtics basketball.. They can use the boos as motivation to play even harder. Coaching – Joe Mazzulla is in his 5th season as Celtics’ head coach. He won a title in 2024 with a very talented team that was packed with shooting stars. Now he has to win in a different way since his personnel has changed and so far he is doing a good job. Nick Nurse is in his 9th season as a head coach overall and his 4th as the 76ers head coach. He won a title with the Raptors in 2019. Nurse came out ahead in the playoffs last season. Can Mazzulla win this round? Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. Every crew officiates differently. Some call it tight, others let them play. The Celtics need to adjust to how the refs are calling the game and not allow bad calls or no calls to take away their focus from playing the game. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid flopping, off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws, and illegal screens. They have been especially calling flops and push offs and so the Celtics need to make an effort to avoid doing both.

stories.title: Game Preview: Phoenix aims to bounce back vs. Clippers
stories.summary: The Suns will look to bounce back in the second of a back-to-back vs. Los Angeles.
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Devin Booker #1 of the Phoenix Suns looks to pass the ball during the game against the LA Clippers on November 8, 2025 at Intuit Dome in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2025 NBAE (Photo by Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Who : Phoenix Suns (3-6) vs. Los Angeles Clippers (2-7) When : 7:00 pm Arizona Time Where : Mortgage Matchup Center — Phoenix, Arizona Watch : Suns+, 3TV/AZFS Listen : KMVP 98.7 The Phoenix Suns will need to have a short memory after being dominated by Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs last night. Wemby walked into our building and dropped 40, 11, and nine blocks in 25 minutes without breaking a sweat. Spurs 122, Suns 96. It was a rough night. But the silver lining is that the starters were on the bench with 9:34 left. Because tonight they have the second of a back-to-back, and tired legs cannot be an excuse. The mood in this fanbase right now is somewhere between “burn it down” and “it’s November, relax.” The Suns sit at 3-6. They’re 2-2 on this seven-game homestand. The two-game win streak over Houston and Orlando either becomes a distant memory (after a loss) or a building block if they win, because then it’s suddenly ”they’ve won 3 of their last 4 games”. So which is it? Make no mistake about it… this is a MUST-WIN game for the Suns. These are the teams you need to beat. Game day in The Valley 🏜️ 🆚 @LAClippers 📍 @Match_Mortgage Center 🕖 7PM 📺 @azfamily | Pregame 6:30PM 📻 @AZSports | @az_mejor 💻 https://t.co/Emsdr8jtHo 🎟️ https://t.co/EBTFhhgmwm pic.twitter.com/zcbodzAR4X — Phoenix Suns (@Suns) November 10, 2026 Tale of the Tape Probable Starters Phoenix Suns G Devin Booker G Jalen Green F Dillon Brooks F Miles Bridges C Oso Ighodaro LA Clippers G Darius Garland G Kris Dunn F Derrick Jones Jr. F Rui Hachimura C Brook Lopez Ingram and Beal are still out, so expect LA to run back the same five that started Sunday in their win over the Pelicans. Injury Report Goody is back! Suns injury report vs. Clippers: OUT: Mark Williams (left shoulder surgery). Jordan Goodwin (right calf injury management) is no longer on the injury report after missing last four games. #Suns — Duane Rankin (@DuaneRankin) November 10, 2026 Suns Mark Williams — OUT (Left Shoulder Surgery) Clippers Brandon Ingram — OUT (Achilles) Bradley Beal — OUT (Knee) What to Watch For Devin Booker needs help, and he needs it from the starters. Book went 10-for-17 for 32 last night. The other four starters combined for 27 points on 10-of-36 shooting. That’s 27.8%. Phoenix shot 39.3% as a team. Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges have to be the second and third options tonight, or this turns into another Booker solo show that ends in a loss. Hunt the Clippers’ second unit . LA snapped a seven-game skid Sunday by beating New Orleans 139-123, and the bench won that game: 59 points and 14 assists from the reserves. Gradey Dick went 6-for-7. Top-5 pick Keaton Wagler hit 3 of 4 from deep in 18 minutes. Wagler also picked up five fouls. That unit is 4th in bench scoring per game, but defensively they have some flaws. Attack, attack, attack. Garland is the engine without Ingram. Darius Garland went for 24 and 10 against the Pelicans. Brook Lopez added 20. Brandon Ingram (heel) and Bradley Beal (knee) are both out tonight. Gillespie, Goodwin and Green have to make Garland work on the ball, and whoever draws Lopez has to drag him out to the perimeter, where his feet are slow. Key to a Suns Win Rebounding is going to be the key for every Suns game, as the Spurs outrebounded them by twenty, 55 to 35. LA shot 55% from the field (46 of 84), went 16-for-38 from three, and piled up 34 assists against 11 turnovers in their win over the Pelicans. They lived at the line, too: 31 of 38 from the line while the Pelicans committed 29 fouls. The glass was basically even, 36-35 Clippers, with LA grabbing 13 offensive boards. Bench Mob The starters held serve, every one of them finishing between +2 and +9. The bench blew it open. Max Strus and Gradey Dick were both +17, Kobe Sanders was +15, and Keaton Wagler was +11. LA won the fourth quarter 37-28. Collin Gillespie, anyone? It’s been a rough season for him, and boy could they use a breakout game in this one from him, not only for his confidence, but to outduel the Clippers’ bench. Jordan Goodwin is back as well, so that hopefully provides a spark. Do not take them lightly. The Clippers are 2nd in the NBA in 3PT% and 4th in bench scoring. Despite their flaws and 7-game losing streak, they are fully capable of getting hot from deep and stealing this one. View Link Prediction The Suns bounce back, and their offense breaks out in a win over the Clippers. We enter the 10-game mark at 4-6, with mixed reviews, but ultimately trending in the right direction, winning 3 of 4. Suns 127, Clippers 115

stories.title: NBA buzz: Latest on trades, news, roster moves and intel
stories.summary: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
stories.detailText: The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders. Quick links: Free agency grades | Trade grades Transactions | Offseason buzz ESPN's new NBA Trade Lab: Swing a deal! Nov. 10 Brown last talked to Tatum in June to discuss future ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the last time Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum spoke was in June after the Boston Celtics failed to trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo . Brown confronted Tatum at a dinner in France about their future as teammates, per Charania. The former teammates will meet for the first time Tuesday night, as the Celtics head to Philadelphia (8 p.m. ET). NBA Trade Lab updates: How could the Lakers level up? The Los Angeles Lakers find themselves at the top of the Western Conference standings, with Luka Doncic playing like the best player in the world and leading the way in ESPN's Net Points Metric . Their projected win total from ESPN's Basketball Power Index that started the season at 45 has already increased to 53. They completely retooled their roster this past offseason after losing LeBron James in free agency to the Philadelphia 76ers , but their newly added pieces have jelled together quickly to leave fans around the league rethinking what the ceiling of this team could be. After sending out two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the Walker Kessler sign-and-trade , the Lakers are very limited in remaining draft capital they could use to add another major piece through a trade. However, this hasn't stopped Lakers fans from diving into our NBA Trade Lab tool to cook up some mock trades in an attempt to find the Lakers another piece around the margins that could complete this roster for a deep playoff run. Trade No. 1: Lakers bring in Luka's former teammate Lakers get: P.J. Washington Dallas Mavericks get: Jarred Vanderbilt , Cameron Carr , and two second-round picks Washington is a versatile two-way wing who started alongside Doncic during the Mavericks' run to the finals in 2024. Washington played the best basketball of his career alongside Luka during their time together on the Mavs and would be a proven contributor to add to the Lakers' depth. Carr, the 24th overall pick in the 2026 draft, is a promising young player the Mavericks can plug in right away and develop around their young core. The two second-round picks would also be a welcome addition for Dallas, which currently doesn't have any second-round picks (outside of a top-55 protected Hawks' 2027 second-rounder). Trade No. 2: L.A. adds a big man Lakers get: Jalen Smith Chicago Bulls get: Jaden Hardy and two second-round picks Smith is a young intriguing stretch big, whose advanced metrics paint as a positive player even on a middling Bulls team. Despite averaging only 17 minutes a game in his career, Smith possesses a rare blend of rim defense, rebounding and 3-point shooting. This would be a buy-low opportunity for the Lakers to invest in the potential of Smith, letting him play off one of the best playmakers in the world in Luka Doncic . Oct. 16 Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions. Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge. For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season. The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET. Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama , Amen and Ausar Thompson , Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023. Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace . Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility. The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks Read more: Which NBA deals will get done? Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Oct. 1 Duren, Pistons end standoff with long-term deal All-NBA center Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons , his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania. Duren had until 11:59 p.m. ET Thursday to decide on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan. "I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year." Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4). Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games. A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder , after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season. Sept. 30 Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived. Sept. 29 Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN. Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal? On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vince Goodwill, Jamal Collier, Anthony Slater and Michael C. Wright all hop on the podcast to discuss the biggest storylines throughout the NBA ahead of training camp. Topics: 01:08: 76ers Media Day reactions 06:55: How LeBron is assimilating in Philadelphia 15:00: How will the 76ers deploy their talent this year? 18:45: Vibes exceedingly high for the Lakers 32:25: Bronny's quotes about LeBron leaving 35:20: Windy Storytime: Bronny's name origins 40:20: Exciting summer coming to a close for the Knicks 41:15: Major contract negotiations ongoing with NY 55:10: Assessing vibes with new pieces in Minnesota 1:08:40: Bad news continues for the Clippers 1:24:15: Evaluating Kawhi's fit with the Raptors 1:30:20: Not a lot of love in the air for Pistons 1:44:30: Breaking down state of the Warriors 2:00:25: Thunder dealing with departure of key teammates 2:16:13: Interesting quotes from Spurs about their starting 5 Goodwill on the latest between the Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns: "It wasn't so much what he said, like this full-throated defense of himself, but he said, 'I would like to get my contract done.' "He said, 'I would like to stay in New York for the rest of my career.' And then he kind of ended it and because of the way the Knicks operated, it wasn't like you had space for a follow-up. "And then someone else, I think Ian Begley asked him, 'Are you OK with playing this out through the season or do you want to table contract talks?' and he basically said, 'Everybody's going to be a little uncomfortable around here.'" Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.title: Warriors blow out Pelicans by 51 points for 8th straight win
stories.summary: Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg added 23 points, and the Warriors won their eighth straight game by 51 points against the short-handed Pelicans on Monday night.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO -- Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the short-handed New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87 victory Monday night -- the largest win by any team this season. It was the Warriors' fourth-largest win in franchise history, and the Pelicans' largest loss in team history. Brandin Podziemski added 25 points, and Curry shot 6 for 10 with four 3-pointers after his 41-point performance in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win against Orlando . He passed DeMar DeRozan (26,800) for 16th place on the NBA's career scoring list with 26,803. Injured guard Jimmy Butler dressed up as a member of the coaching staff and held a clipboard, writing "PASS TO STEPH" on it. As Warriors coach Steve Kerr later explained: "It was funny because I don't know how this happened, but I told [assistant coach] Khalid [Robinson] about five minutes before the game, I told Khalid, 'One of these days, we should have Jimmy dress up like us' because he's always got some great outfit on and something fashionable, and we wear our quarter-zips and sweaters. I said, 'We should really get him to dress like a coach one day,' and then he walks out, and he's dressed like us. I turned to Khalid, I said, 'Did you tell him to do that?' and he goes, 'No.' It was, I guess, mental telepathy or something. We're on the same page on that. He was enjoying himself." As for what he made of Butler's coaching prospects, Kerr acknowledged, "He said all the right things, you know, team fouls, you know, how many team fouls we had, like he was really acting the part." That being said, "I also realized he was mocking us" -- with Kerr later citing the "PASS TO STEPH" board that he didn't know about until after the game. Lendeborg was also asked for his verdict on "Coach Jimmy" and did not hold back: "I didn't learn anything. All I learned was once you're on the court with Stephen Curry, give Stephen Curry the ball. That's all I learned. Bad coaching by him, man." In a postgame interview with NBC Sports Bay Area, Lendeborg also noted that Butler "said he was going to get a tech for us tonight. He didn't, so ... shame on him." Still, Lendeborg has appreciated Butler's wisdom while he recovers from surgery in February on his right knee for a torn anterior cruciate ligament. "For me especially, he's always just giving me little tips and tricks on the court," Lendeborg said. Golden State had three players with at least 20 points for the second time this season, and the Warriors finished with 30 or more assists -- 37 -- for the third straight game and fifth in the past six matchups. They are 6-0 when doing so. It was the largest win by the Warriors since April 9, 2023, at Portland (+56), and Golden State's largest home win since Nov. 2, 1991, against the Kings (+62). Derik Queen scored 16 points off the bench, and Dejounte Murray added 12 points for the Pelicans, who were out of the game almost from the tipoff and trailed 72-43 at halftime on the way to losing a third straight after a four-game winning streak. Golden State led 35-20 after one quarter as New Orleans shot just 7 of 23 and missed 10 of 12 3-point tries. The Warriors built a 23-point lead early in the second quarter as Podziemski scored four quick points and rolled from there. Charles Bassey contributed 12 points and 10 rebounds off the bench, and De'Anthony Melton scored 16 with four 3s in the win. Lendeborg and Pelicans guard Jordan Poole , both former Michigan stars, traded jerseys afterward. New Orleans rested Zion Williamson a night after a 139-123 road loss to the Clippers , and Trey Murphy III also sat out to manage his troublesome knees after he scored 26 in Los Angeles on Sunday. The Warriors have won eight straight after starting 0-3, which is the second-longest win streak after an 0-3 (or worse) start to a season in NBA history. The 2006-07 Mavericks started 0-4 and then won 12 straight. ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 9: Collin Sexton #10 of the Los Angeles Lakers drives to the basket during the game against the Atlanta Hawks on November 9, 2026 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Joe Boatman/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Over the past two games, Collin Sexton has been indispensable in powering the Los Angeles Lakers to wins with their star guards, Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves, each missing one contest. Against the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, the veteran guard tallied 17 points (5-of-10 shooting), two assists and two rebounds. A day later, he followed that up with 18 points (6-of-11 shooting), six assists, two rebounds and one steal in Monday’s win over the Atlanta Hawks . If those consecutive performances are any indication, Sexton could be finding his footing after a slow start to 2026-27, which featured a calf strain that hampered him during training camp and preseason. Through his first nine appearances, he averaged 8.7 points while shooting 40% from the floor and 25.8% from deep (49.5% true shooting). In this week’s pair of victories, he’s averaged 17.5 points on 52.4% shooting and 50% from deep (64.4% true shooting). Following those laudatory outings, Sexton said he feels he’s inching closer to fully being himself again. “I think maybe another week and a half, two weeks and I think I’ll be back,“ he told reporters Monday. ”Right now, these last two games felt really good. So I’m moving in the right direction.” As Sexton works to rediscover his rhythm, he’s embracing patience. “That’s one word I’ve been using each and every day,” he said. “I would say each and every day is going to have its ups, have its downs but I’m blessed to be healthy enough to go out.” JJ Redick mentioned pregame that he uses the word "patience" with Collin Sexton. Collin on how challenging it's been being patient after being sidelined for several weeks during training camp/preseason with a calf strain: "That's one word I've been using each and every day…I… pic.twitter.com/MNFcjrwxcA — Khobi Price (@khobi_price) November 10, 2026 Head coach JJ Redick is counting on Sexton to help steady second units for the Lakers, given he’s their most talented scorer and qualified initiator off the bench. After Monday’s win, he spoke about Sexton’s role in keeping the offense humming when the speedy guard is at the forefront. “I think the biggest thing [is] we’re trying to get organized and and there’s glimpses of really good organization when he’s out there as the primary ball handler,” Redick told reporters. “We got a little squirrely there at the end of the second quarter. I thought, for the most part, outside of the first few minutes in that third quarter where I had to call the early timeout, I thought we did a good job of just being organized and trying to get good shots. That’s how you end up with 124 points against a good team.” You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Sixers tease Celtics with 'Why Can't We Be Friends' amid Tatum-Brown feud
stories.summary: The 76ers couldn't resist having a little fun with the ongoing Jayson Tatum-Jaylen Brown drama before Tuesday's showdown against the Celtics.
stories.detailText: The anticipation continues to build for the first game between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers since their offseason trade that sent Jaylen Brown to the Sixers. The two teams play Tuesday, Nov. 10 , in a matchup the entire NBA will be focused on because of the brewing feud between Brown and Celtics star Jayson Tatum after the two former teammates parted ways. So the Sixers decided to have a little fun with the growing controversy when the Celtics took the floor for their morning shootaround at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. The song, "Why Can't We Be Friends?" by War played on the public address system as the 76ers were on the court, according to video taken by reporters in attendance. Brown and Tatum spent nine seasons together with the Celtics and won an NBA championship in 2022. But their fruitful on-court partnership has devolved into a war of words off the floor now that they're on rival teams. WHERE'S THE BEEF? First Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown showdown could offer early scorecard Brown raised the temperature significantly last month with two public reveals regarding the offseason move. He initially posted an emoji of a blue hat – which is another way to say cap, or slang that someone is being dishonest – to a video on social media in which Tatum said he was caught off guard by the July trade. Brown then told reporters on Oct. 24 , "There’s no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy, and he should stay ready at all times." Tatum has attempted to downplay the rift and initially responded to Brown's comments by emphasizing , "This ain’t no (expletive) Shaq and Kobe. It’s not about that." The two nonetheless appeared to avoid each other when the Sixers and Celtics met in the preseason. Brown did not play in the Oct. 16 exhibition game, but both players warmed up on opposite sides of the floor and did not acknowledge each other, at least not publicly. Despite winning a title together, speculation about the partnership followed them throughout much of their time in Boston. Tensions between the former teammates intensified after Brown became a fixture in offseason trade rumors. When the Celtics ultimately dealt him to Philadelphia in a blockbuster move, the spotlight on his relationship with Tatum only grew. The Sixers are off to a 9-2 start heading into Tuesday's game, and acquiring Brown helped convince LeBron James to sign with Philadelphia over several other suitors. The Celtics, who got Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the deal, are right below the Sixers in the Eastern Conference standings with Tatum averaging more than 27 points per game and on pace to set a career high for assists. The good vibes and serious undertones made the Sixers' attempt at comic relief during shootaround feel all the more appropriate. Watch what happened here: Hilarious music choice as the Celtics wait to begin shootaround. pic.twitter.com/HBTA2MhTCW — Jay King (@ByJayKing) November 10, 2026 Celtics shootaround underway with “why can’t we be friends” playing. pic.twitter.com/EJV3A8pQKL — Bobby Manning (@RealBobManning) November 10, 2026 The music at #Celtics shootaround: War’s “Why Can’t We Be Friends?” And that’s not an accident. #76ers . pic.twitter.com/s4Ielx5yzJ — gary washburn (@GwashburnGlobe) November 10, 2026 This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Sixers tease Celtics with 'Why Can't We Be Friends' amid Tatum-Brown feud

stories.summary: Los Angeles received key contributions from various role players to win Sunday and Monday
stories.detailText: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 09: Head coach JJ Redick of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on against the Atlanta Hawks during the fourth quarter at State Farm Arena on November 09, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite missing Luka Dončić Sunday against the Detroit Pistons and Austin Reaves Monday against the Atlanta Hawks, the Los Angeles Lakers went on the road for a back-to-back set and won both games over two of the Eastern Conference’s top-four seeds. On Sunday, Reaves’ 43 points led the Lakers while Dončić‘s 32-point, 10-assist double-double paced them Monday night. But in both outings, Los Angeles’ depth played crucial roles to fill the void vacated by the absence of a star guard. Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams all delivered, helping propel Los Angeles to a pair of impressive road victories — and head coach JJ Redick recognized their efforts. “I think the last two games, great examples of next guy up,” Redick told reporters postgame Monday. “…I thought Collin did a really nice job of attacking the paint and scoring. Giving us some juice, especially there in the first half. Sandro, his best game as a Laker and whatever he had, 23 points. That was awesome. Made some big time plays. I thought the two defensive rebounds he got there in the last few minutes were as big as any play he made all night.” Walker Kessler filled up the stat sheet across both games, averaging 16.5 points, 13 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 2.0 blocks and 1.0 steals to fortify the interior on both ends. His rebounding, finishing, rim protection and quick decision-making are integral to Los Angeles’ 10-2 start this season. Of course, Dončić and Reaves will shepherd the Lakers’ success — as they have through three weeks — but the supporting cast members elevating their play when called upon will be necessary if the Lakers are to contend for a title. “It’s building resiliency. JJ talks about it, going through adversity, and understanding that, to be a championship team, you’ve got to respond to that kind of stuff,” Kessler said Monday. “When they made their fourth quarter run, we responded accordingly and got the win.” Los Angeles will look to extend its winning streak to seven games and maintain an undefeated road trip when it faces the Milwaukee Bucks Wednesday night. Tipoff is scheduled for 5 p.m. PST. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .
