stories.title: Jimmy Butler’s hysterical ‘coaching’ debut draws wild reaction in 51-point win: ‘He trippin’
stories.summary: After Jimmy Butler's coaching debut on the Warriors bench, at least one teammate would prefer he sticks to his day job(s).
stories.detailText: Coffee connoisseur. Domino don. Coach Jimmy? Jimmy Butler has no shortage of hobbies and side gigs to keep him busy even while unable to get on the court for the Warriors while rehabbing the ACL he tore in January. He added another Monday night, to the amusement of his Golden State teammates . At least one of them would prefer to see Butler stick to his dayjob(s), though. “Man, nah, nah, nah. He gotta go home,” Warriors guard De’Anthony Melton told the NBC Sports Bay Area broadcast following the 138-87 win over the Pelicans. “The next time he do something like that, he gotta go back home or do something else. Because he trippin’.” De'Anthony Melton on Jimmy with the clipboard: "He gotta go home. Next time he do something like that, he need to go back home or do something else because he trippin" pic.twitter.com/Xda4VyXRrg https://t.co/bsKv9jX4iE — Oh No He Didn't (@ohnohedidnt24) November 10, 2026 De’Anthony Melton of the Golden State Warriors speaks to the media after a game against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. NBAE via Getty Images Melton was on the receiving end of Butler’s most pointed coaching advice of the night. Taking his usual seat on the bench, Butler traded in his typically fashion-forward wardrobe for a white pullover and black joggers — the same get-up as Steve Kerr and the rest of the Warriors coaching staff . He also grabbed a clipboard, which came in handy to remind Melton of the golden rule of basketball in Golden State: Pass the ball to Steph Curry . When Melton checked out midway through the third quarter, Butler spelled it out loud and clear in blue ink on the clipboard and held it up for Melton — and the cameras — to see. Georges Niang, left, and Jimmy Butler III smile after a game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Melton had just violated the one and only edict on two possessions in quick succession. Curry was open on the perimeter but Melton drove to the rim through traffic and failed to convert. Butler offered him — and the rest of the Warriors — a simple reminder. “All I learned is once you’re on the court with Steph, give Steph the ball,” rookie Yaxel Lendeborg said of Butler as a tactician. “Just get the ball to Steph. That’s the most serious thing he said.” Stephen Curry (30) of the Golden State Warriors prepares to shoot against the New Orleans Pelicans on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. Getty Images Butler gave his teammates no advance notice of his plans for the game. Lendeborg even mistook him for a regular member of the coaching staff at first. “I think it was during the first timeout. I was walking by, going to ask coach Frank (Vogel) a question and I see Jimmy. Like, what? What are you wearing?” Lendeborg chuckled. “I didn’t realize all the coaches wear the same thing until today.” Butler’s wardrobe ensured that he would blend right in on the bench. “I thought he looked great. Really good-looking sweater,” Kerr quipped. “He said all the right things. Team fouls. How many team fouls we had. He was really acting the part. But I also realized he was mocking us, so it hurt a little bit.” “HE WAS REALLY ACTING THE PART… BUT I ALSO REALIZED HE WAS MOCKING US.” Steve Kerr provides his honest evaluation of Jimmy Butler III's coaching performance in last night's win https://t.co/bajs9ItmK9 pic.twitter.com/IpBemMafvE — NBA (@NBA) November 10, 2026 It was all in good fun, but Melton agreed: he preferred Butler on the court than the bench. “No. Just no,” Melton said with a laugh when asked about Butler’s coaching debut. “I think he just got fired today, which is actually crazy. I’m happy about that.”

stories.title: Views from the Game: Rockets defeat Nuggets 110-100; TDS speaks with Kevin Durant, Alperen Sengun
stories.summary: The Rockets beat the Nuggets, and TDS spoke to Houston’s two stars.
stories.detailText: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 09: Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets and Alperen Sengun #28 of the Houston Rockets embrace during the second half against the Denver Nuggets at Toyota Center on November 09, 2026 in Houston, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Rockets faced the Denver Nuggets in unfamiliar territory on Monday. The Rockets entered Monday night’s game on their first two-game losing streak of the season after their 102-99 loss to the Phoenix Suns on Saturday. In that game, the Rockets struggled from the field as the Suns led by double digits in the first quarter. The Rockets eventually got back in the game and even took a six-point lead at one point in the second half. Still, even a fourth-quarter resurgence from Alperen Sengun, who struggled the first three quarters, wasn’t enough to keep the Rockets from dropping their second straight game. Pregame The Rockets welcomed the Nuggets, who are coming off a win down in Mexico City over the Los Angeles Clippers. The Rockets have been without Steven Adams and Clint Capela for several games and also added Oscar Tshiebwe to their injury report with an illness. That means the Rockets will be without all three of their backup centers, leaving Sengun as the only active center for Monday’s game. Ime Udoka did mention how both Steven Adams and Clint Capela are targeting the upcoming road trip, specifically the Washington and Miami games, as possible return dates. That would be a welcome sight for a Rockets team that currently ranks 12th in rebounding after being near or at the top every season of Ime Udoka’s Rockets tenure. Rockets vs Nuggets The Rockets got off to a fast start, led by Durant, who made his first three shots, including one from beyond the arc. Durant was as aggressive in the first quarter as he has been in several games. The quarter was back and forth, as neither team could get much separation. The Nuggets started to take advantage of the Rockets’ lack of depth at center as Jokic went to work once Sengun went to the bench. However, the Rockets put together a good finish to the quarter, and a Tari Eason 3-pointer put them up 32-24 at the end of the first quarter. Durant led all scorers with 11 points in the first 12 minutes. The Rockets carried that momentum into the second quarter, scoring the first 11 points and building a lead of as much as 19. The Rockets played with much more force and composure than in their first half against the Suns. The Rockets had 13 assists out of their first 20 made baskets. The Rockets maintained the lead, taking a 54-40 lead into halftime. The third quarter saw the Nuggets cut the lead to under double digits early as they started the quarter on fire from the field. The Rockets, meanwhile, saw their shooting fall off a cliff, starting 2-for-14 from the field as the Nuggets came back from an early 18-point deficit to tie the game at 5:02. That’s when Marcus Smart and Tari Eason entered the game, and the Rockets’ defensive intensity immediately rose. The Rockets strung together good defensive possessions that led to easy baskets and pushed the lead back to nine at 71-62. Despite a rough start to the quarter, the Rockets led 77-68 heading into the fourth quarter. In the fourth quarter, both teams played at a high level for the first time. On one end, Sengun scored in the paint; on the other, Jamal Murray could not miss from mid-range. The Rockets had a slim six-point lead midway through the fourth quarter. That’s when Sengun took over: he not only scored in the paint to give the Rockets a 98-90 lead, but he also assisted on the next two baskets, helping the Rockets put the game away with a 110-100 win. The win snapped the Rockets’ first two-game losing streak of the season. Postgame: After the game, Ime Udoka, Kevin Durant, and Alperen Sengun spoke to the media. Udoka said the Rockets did a much better job taking care of the basketball and distributing it, and that they finished with 29 assists. SB Nation asked Durant whether it is easier to figure out the defense when he’s initiating the offense. KD finished with a season high 8 assists I asked KD if it is easier for him sometimes to see how a defense wants to guard him. “I'm better up there. When I am running off the pin downs I am cool to but like you said I don't know where the defense is.” pic.twitter.com/e78K9KiIb2 — Lachard Binkley (@BinkleyHoops) November 10, 2026 Sengun helped close out the Nuggets with his own great passing and running the pick-and-roll with Durant. Here are both players praising each other’s games after last night’s win. Kevin Durant and Alperen Sengun each had high praise for the other after last night's win. KD on AlP play “To be honest I feel like everytime I have been playing with him about 95, 96 percent of the time he makes a solid decision.” AlP on KD “He made really good reads today… pic.twitter.com/CxWGPBCQYu — Lachard Binkley (@BinkleyHoops) November 10, 2026 The Rockets now begin preparing for their old nemesis, Steph Curry and the Golden State Warriors, who come to town Wednesday with an 8-3 record and have won their last eight games.

stories.title: ‘Thank goodness he’s on our team’: Cooper Flagg makes history, Dallas Mavericks keep stacking wins
stories.summary: Flagg's historic 43-point night and Irving's 35 on the second night of a back-to-back pushed Dallas to 7-4, and a battered fan base finally has something real to believe in.
stories.detailText: With the Dallas Mavericks down 13 points late in the first half on the second night of a back-to-back, Monday night at American Airlines Center looked very much like a schedule loss. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving had other ideas, though, as they combined for 78 points, fueling Dallas past the Indiana Pacers in a wild finish, 125-122 . The win was the Mavericks’ third straight and moved Dallas to 7-4 on the season. It also put the Mavs three games over .500 for the first time since March 1, 2025, a date that feels a lot longer ago than it actually is for anyone who has lived through the last two years of Mavericks basketball. Think about where this franchise was not long ago. The Luka Doncic trade. Irving’s torn ACL. A 26-56 season and back-to-back years without a playoff appearance. Oddsmakers set Dallas’ win total at 34.5 before this season, and after an opening stretch that included Houston, San Antonio and Oklahoma City, a lot of people expected the Mavs to be scrapping just to stay afloat by mid-November. Instead, the Mavs are stacking wins, Flagg looks like an MVP candidate in year two, and Irving looks like his old self before the ACL injury happened. Most importantly, the way the Mavs are winning these games feels sustainable. Here are some of the biggest storylines from Monday night’s thriller. Flagg Climbs Even Higher in the Teenage Record Books DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks dunks during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Flagg was good in the first half, but he was on an entirely different level in the second. The 19-year-old star scored 30 of his season-high 43 points after halftime, including 14 on 6-of-6 shooting in the third quarter and 16 more in the fourth. He finished 16-of-25 from the field, 3-of-6 from 3-point range and a perfect 8-of-8 at the free-throw line, adding 10 rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block for his fourth straight double-double. Flagg became just the second teenager in NBA history to post at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game, joining Kevin Durant, who put up 42 points, 13 rebounds and six assists in the final game of his rookie season with Seattle in 2008. Per StatMuse, add the three steals, and Flagg is the first teenager ever with a 40-10-5-3 line. It was also his fifth career 40-point game, as many as the next two teenagers on that list combined (LeBron James with three and Anthony Edwards with two). His 14th career 30-point game moved him into second place for the most by a player under 20, behind only James, and his seventh 35-point game tied James for the most by a teenager. And keep in mind, Flagg doesn’t turn 20 until Dec. 21. Mavericks head coach Dusty May pointed to how complete Flagg’s scoring package has become. “He gets to the rim,” May said in his postgame media availability. “I think him almost being a left-handed player in the paint certainly helps. He’s a great left-footed jumper, left-handed finisher. Then he’s able to square in the air from 15, 17 feet. … The last couple of games, he’s made some threes and he’s making all of his free throws. That’s how you put up the 43 points, where you do a little bit of everything.” It’s almost unreal just how good Flagg already is, and May is just happy he’s on his roster and not having to gameplan against him. “He affects the game in so many ways and he makes the right plays as far as passing,” May said. “Thank goodness he’s on our team. It’s unbelievable that he’s a 19-year-old doing this.” Flagg’s deadly midrange shot, which he worked on all offseason, is paying off in a big way, especially in clutch situations, where he leads the league in clutch points. “I think just being able to get to my spots at a higher level and being more comfortable with that has allowed me to take a little bit of load off my body,” Flagg said. “Just kind of stopping short, raising up over people. It’s taxing going downhill all the way to the rim and trying to finish over seven-footers all night, every night. … Just trusting the work, trusting the spot work that I put in all summer long.” Through 11 games, the reigning Rookie of the Year is averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.2 steals per game. Again, given everything Mavs fans have been through over the last 21 months, this sort of euphoric rise back to genuine happiness watching these games is hard to believe. Irving looks sharp on night 2 of a back-to-back DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates after scoring a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images Flagg was the closer on Monday night, but Irving was arguably the reason Dallas was still in the game in those closing moments. Playing the second night of a back-to-back for the first time this season, a day after logging 28 minutes in a 130-93 win over Brooklyn, Irving poured in 35 points in a season-high 38 minutes. He knocked down a season-high seven 3-pointers on 10 attempts, went 3-of-3 at the line and finished a game-best plus-29. After missing 19 months with the torn ACL he suffered in March 2025, Irving said he told his teammates in the locker room after Sunday’s win that he planned to play. “When you’re in a combative sport such as basketball, some days are going to feel good, some days aren’t, especially coming off an injury or a long period of time,” Irving said. “So I just had to get my body back used to being in the flow of the game. … I was just feeling great, and just coming in to today.” May, who said plus-minus is often overblown in a one-game sample, made an exception for Irving in this one. “His plus-29 tonight was very indicative of how important he is,” May said. “When we were struggling to make shots in the first half, we thought we were generating really good looks. We just looked a little bit flat. I thought Kyrie’s shot-making just kind of righted the ship for us.” It’s still early, but seeing Irving look this healthy and proving to be a seamless fit next to Flagg bodes well for what this team can accomplish this year. Perhaps the last two years of the basketball injury gods punishing the Mavs will result in some good injury luck the rest of this season. A star pairing without the ego DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates with teammate Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks after scoring a basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The most encouraging part of all of this is just how naturally Flagg and Irving shared the scoring load against Indiana. The two combined for 26 fourth-quarter points, including Dallas’ first 13 of the period, and May said neither player blinks when the play call goes to the other. “We’re coming out of a timeout, we may draw up a play for one of them just because the other one might have an All-League defender on him, or whatever the case, and they never roll their eyes,” May said. “They know when we’re going to one of the two, the other one’s very, very supportive because they have that much respect for each other.” Irving, an established champion who has shared the floor with more than a few superstars over his 15-year career, is grateful that he’s able to be Flagg’s teammate, despite the two players being on different ends of their careers. “We keep calling him a teenager, but he plays way beyond his years. We’ve got to give him his flowers,” Irving said. “Most young guys will probably move away from that contact, but it seems like this newer generation that’s coming into our league, they fear nothing. And I think he falls right in line with that. So grateful to have him on the wing with me.” Those feelings are mutual for Flagg: “Just having [Kyrie] out there, his gravity opening the floor for everybody else, it makes my life so much easier.” Surviving a chaotic finish DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: P.J. Washington #25 of the Dallas Mavericks celebrates a three point basket during the second half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t pretty at the end, but it didn’t have to be for the Mavs to come up with another win. That’s one thing that’s been so encouraging about this fast start to the season. Dallas is finding different ways to win, whether it’s pretty or not. Indiana’s Pascal Siakam torched Dallas for 26 first-half points on 8-of-9 shooting, but the Mavs adjusted their help defense after the break and held him to just three points on 1-of-7 shooting the rest of the way. The Pacers took a 66-56 lead into halftime and a 93-90 lead into the fourth before Flagg buried a 26-foot pull-up 3 to tie it. Irving’s 23-footer with 9:36 left put Dallas in front for good. Leading 125-122 with a chance to put the game on ice, PJ Washington missed a pair of free throws with four seconds left, and Caleb Martin bailed everyone out by stealing Andrew Nembhard’s inbounds pass to Siakam with 0.9 seconds remaining. Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle was adamant that Martin fouled Siakam on that final play, but judging from the replays, it looked like Martin got all ball before ever making any contact with Siakam. It obviously would’ve been nice for Washington to sink at least one of those free throws to avoid that last-second drama, but again, the Mavs keep finding different ways to win. How many times over the past two years have we seen a game like that end in a loss for Dallas? Permission to dream a little? DALLAS, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 9: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks goes to the basket during the first half against the Indiana Pacers at American Airlines Center on November 9, 2026 in Dallas, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images As good (and fun) as the Mavs have been early on, Irving knows his team still has a long way to go to get to the level they want to be at. “We haven’t earned anything in this league yet,” Irving said. “We consistently do it every night, and that’s how you build your identity in this league and you earn your respect. We try not to put the cart before the horse.” With that being said, though, Mavs fans have earned the right to enjoy this start and, dare I say, dream big again. After two years of nothing but gut punches, a 7-4 start built on a generational teenager, a healthy veteran star and a team that genuinely seems to like playing together is a foundation Mavs fans have been waiting on. Irving acknowledged the preseason doubt, saying the team heard “a lot of the noise” and chose not to let outside voices into the locker room. If he keeps playing like prime Kyrie, though, and if Flagg keeps rewriting the record books at this current pace, those voices of doubt are going to continue to get a whole lot quieter. The Mavericks will now hit the road for a big three-game trip that will show just how real this start is, beginning Thursday against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center at 7 p.m. CT. Dallas then visits the Cleveland Cavaliers on Nov. 14 and the Boston Celtics on Nov. 15.

stories.title: Paul George treating return to Philly as “a regular game”
stories.summary: Paul George returns to Xfinity Mobile Arena after two seasons as a 76er.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - APRIL 30: Jayson Tatum #0, Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics and Paul George #8 of the Philadelphia 76ers looks on during the game during Round One Game Six of the 2026 NBA Playoffs on April 30, 2026 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by David Dow/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Lost in the background of the highly anticipated first matchup between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum is a return to Philadelphia for Paul George, who spent his past two seasons as a Sixer. Both Brown and Tatum have downplayed the narrative, as hard as it is to ignore. George, who played 89 games in a Sixers uniform, is following suit. “It’s a regular game — that’s how I’m treating it,” he said during Boston’s morning shootaround. George said he was unsure of the reception he’d receive in his first game back to Xfinity Mobile Arena, a place where in his last appearance, he scored a series-best 23 points on 47% efficiency to go with vintage defense, forcing four Celtics turnovers and holding shooters matched up with him to 33% (5/15 FG). It played a part in Philly completing the 14th 3-1 series comeback in NBA history. And yet, George’s brief stint in Philadelphia was defined by a core group that struggled to stay on the floor at the same time, and ran into the same second round demons they’ve yet to exorcise since the beginning of The Process. “Had I been here 8, 9, 10 years it’d be a different story. I was there 2 years,” he said. Interesting perspective from George on the reception he expects in Philadelphia tonight: "Not sure. In some ways, I helped land them a future piece. So with that, I'm not sure how the reception will be." "Was there 2 years. Obviously, we didn't have the best of luck. We had a… — Bobby Manning (@RealBobManning) November 10, 2026 It’s an easy narrative to shrug off for George because, over his 17 seasons, he’s gone through this same thing before. “He said he’s returned to four different teams before. There’s nothing new to him,” Payton Pritchard said. George had his own contentious reunion when he played against the Indiana Pacers for the first time, followed by games against the Thunder and Clippers. George isn’t the only Celtic currently on the roster to have experienced an anticipated reunion between a foundational player and the team that drafted him. Mike Conley, a 12-year Grizzlies mainstay before the organization ended the Grit and Grind with a full scale rebuild, was showered with appreciation and given a hero’s welcome from the Memphis fanbase in his first game against them in 2019. Their experiences couldn’t have been farther apart. In the case of George, whose seven years in Indiana ended in a trade request, he first played the Pacers in Oklahoma City, struggling with foul trouble and playing just 19 minutes in an 18-point win. When he played in Indiana for the first time later that season, he was showered with boos from the moment his name was announced, and he shot just 3-of-14 for 12 points, though a late steal and two clutch free throws contributed to a 100-95 win. “I’m happy this circus is over with. Everybody can move on,” George said after his return to Indiana . The response was different in George’s next stop; he was given a tribute video and crowd ovation playing against the Thunder for the first time. Against the Clippers, a video tribute was also presented, but there was a mix of cheers and boos, a reaction he described as “stupid,” though he cited no ill will towards the franchise or his time spent in Los Angeles. “The boos, I didn’t get it,” he said after his first game against the Clippers . “I still don’t get it when I go [back] to Indy, but it is what it is. It’s sports. I look forward to next year being back here and more boos.” It’s hard to say the exact response when George’s name is called in the lineup introductions tonight. As the Celtics got rolling on their shootaround inside Xfinity Mobile Arena, the song “Why Can’t We Be Friends” by War blared from the speakers, a tongue and cheek choice to kick off what will be one of the most watched and debated rivalry games of the season. Celtics shootaround underway with “why can’t we be friends” playing. pic.twitter.com/EJV3A8pQKL — Bobby Manning (@RealBobManning) November 10, 2026 Perhaps it’s a sign that tempers will be calm on Tuesday night. The game will be played, hands will be shaken, and hugs will be dispersed from competitor to competitor after an early November test between two Eastern Conference contenders. Or maybe that’s just wishful thinking.

stories.title: Lakers ‘registered interest’ in Nique Clifford before trade to Thunder
stories.summary: Los Angeles was one of three other teams besides the Thunder to gauge the market for Clifford
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 10: Nique Clifford #10 of the Sacramento Kings stands on the court during the second half of the preseason game against the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center on October 10, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Godofredo A. Vásquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday afternoon, the Sacramento Kings agreed to deal second-year wing Nique Clifford to the Oklahoma City Thunder in exchange for two second-round picks. Clifford held a fairly sizable role during his rookie season, when he averaged 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 25.1 minutes per game. But he’d fallen out of Sacramento’s rotation to begin 2026-27 and played just 50 minutes in eight games prior to the trade. With the Thunder ravaged by early season injuries , they opted to tap into their surplus of picks and add a reinforcement to their wing room with the hopes he might break out in a more stable organization. Oklahoma City, however, was not the lone playoff hopeful eyeing Clifford. Marc Stein and Jake Fischer reported that a trio of other suitors, including the Los Angeles Lakers, gauged the market for him. Ultimately, though, the Thunder emerged victorious in the Nique Clifford Sweepstakes. “The Pacers, Nuggets and Lakers, sources say, were among the teams that registered trade interest in the 24-year-old,“ according to The Stein Line Substack , “but Oklahoma City had multiple advantages when it came to getting a deal done.” Among the “multiple advantages” referenced there is presumably Oklahoma City’s wealth of picks. Between 2027 and 2033, it owns 15 second-round picks, one of which is Los Angeles’ 2032 second-rounder. For comparison, the Lakers own just three over that same span. Plus, the Lakers are also already fairly well-stocked with youthful wings worth taking a swing on this season. Adou Thiero (22 years old), Cameron Carr (22) and Ziaire Williams (25) are all 25 or younger and have garnered varying levels of rotation minutes to open the year. Given the Lakers’ depleted well of draft capital, it probably didn’t make much sense to fork over two of their remaining three second-round picks through 2033 for a dude who *might* crack the rotation on certain nights. If they’re going to move some of those picks, it should be for someone they know can be a difference-maker and mainstay in the rotation. Clifford, while still pretty young and far from a finished product in the league, certainly does not fit that billing. You can follow Jackson on Twitter at @jackfrank_jjf .

stories.title: Steve Kerr sounds alarm over Warriors’ latest injury: ‘It’s a big concern’
stories.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr speaks to the media before a game against the Miami Heat on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco.The Golden State Warriors have...
stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr speaks to the media before a game against the Miami Heat on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, in San Francisco. The Golden State Warriors have won eight straight games and look like one of the Western Conference’s best teams. But it was not all smiles for Golden State after Monday’s 138-87 win over the New Orleans Pelicans, given the injury that backup point guard Brandon Williams suffered. Warriors head coach Steve Kerr spoke about how much of a blow Williams’ injury is when speaking to the media postgame. Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr speaks to the media during a pregame press conference before a game against the Miami Heat, Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. Yalonda M. James/San Francisco Chronicle via AP “Yeah, it’s a big concern. He’s a huge part of our team, and he’s given us such a lift. And it’s a hamstring. He’s going to get an MRI, so we’ll see how bad it is,” Kerr said on Williams’ injury. Williams has been one of the Warriors’ best surprises this season. He is averaging 10.4 points in 16.1 minutes per game for Golden State after signing a one-year, $2.6 million for them this past offseason. Brandon Williams of the Golden State Warriors handles the ball against the Orlando Magic at Chase Center in San Francisco, California, Nov. 7, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images Brandon Williams (12) of the Golden State Warriors shoots a free throw against the Orlando Magic at Chase Center in San Francisco on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images It’s still too early to tell how long Williams might be sidelined for. But hamstring injuries are notoriously difficult to recover from and have a high risk of re-injury, so Golden State might prefer to be as cautious as possible when easing him back to the court. Injuries might be the only thing that can slow Golden State down right now. Unfortunately, these injuries are appearing at an alarming rate.

stories.title: Tre Johnson is struggling from three. So are the Wizards
stories.summary: DETROIT — Tre Johnson is an elite shooter. It’s why the Washington Wizards selected him No. 6 in the 2025 draft. But his jump shot hasn’t clicked at the start of the 2026-27 season. Johnson scored two points on 1-for-8 shooting in Monday’s 122-111 loss to the Detroit Pistons just two days after shooting 2-for-15 […]
stories.detailText: CHARLOTTE, NC - OCTOBER 26: Tre Johnson #12 of the Washington Wizards looks on during the game against the Charlotte Hornets on October 26, 2026 at Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kent Smith/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images DETROIT — Tre Johnson is an elite shooter. It’s why the Washington Wizards selected him No. 6 in the 2025 draft. But his jump shot hasn’t clicked at the start of the 2026-27 season. Johnson scored two points on 1-for-8 shooting in Monday’s 122-111 loss to the Detroit Pistons just two days after shooting 2-for-15 in a 114-75 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder. Johnson missed all 13 of his 3-point attempts in those contests. He is shooting 35.1% from the field through 11 games. His 24.5% 3-point percentage is the second-worst in the NBA among players with at least 50 3-point attempts this season, trailing only Ace Bailey’s 22.6%. In Monday’s loss, Johnson missed two wide-open triples — one in the far corner and another on the wing — in the first half. In the second half, he missed three more open looks to finish 0-for-6 from long range. His lone make was a 3-foot push shot that rimmed in. Johnson is getting open looks. He’s just missing them. “[Johnson] had a great game in Atlanta the other night. This is what this guy does. I got great faith in him,” Brian Keefe said. “He got some good looks tonight. He’s gonna knock those down. We saw what he did last year with the percentage he shot. That’ll turn. He puts in all the work, and I got great faith in him.” Johnson’s struggles are concerning. But he’s far from the only Wizards with an inefficient 3-ball. The Wizards made just nine of their 36 3-point attempts in Monday’s loss. They’re shooting 29% from three, which ranks 29th in the league. Trae Young made just three of his 10 3-point attempts in Monday’s loss. He’s shooting 28.8% from three. Alex Sarr missed both of his outside jumpers to fall to 19.4% from three this season. Kyshawn George shot just 2-for-6 from long range. Washington has a shooting problem. Keefe believes this slump will pass. But 11 games in, the Wizards’ spacing concerns have been realized. “We’ve got guys who can make them. I’ve got faith in our shooters. We’re in a tough stretch shooting-wise, but these things will average out,” Keefe said. “ We’re going to continue to do the right things, put ourselves in the position to make those shots, and I got faith in our guys.” AJ Dybantsa, who scored 21 points against Detroit but made just one of his four 3-point attempts, reiterated that sentiment. The rookie remained confident in the Wizards’ ability to make open shots, especially from three. “Keep shooting. We’re NBA players. We’re gonna knock shots down,” Dybantsa said. “We might be in a shooting slump right now, but [we] have to keep shooting.”

stories.title: Payton Pritchard, Paul George preview highly anticipated Celtics-76ers matchup
stories.summary: Pritchard shed light on the relationship between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown as the Celtics prepare to take on the 76ers: “There was no beef.”
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MA - FEBRUARY 1: Payton Pritchard #11 and Jaylen Brown #7 of the Boston Celtics high five during the game against the Milwaukee Bucksduring the 2026 NBA Pioneers Classic on February 1, 2026 at TD Garden in Boston, Massachusetts. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Celtics will face an old friend when they take on the 76ers on Tuesday night: Jaylen Brown, who spent a decade in Boston before being traded to Philadelphia on Tuesday. And Payton Pritchard, one of Brown’s longest-tenured teammates, looks forward to the match-up. “I definitely had a lot of good memories with JB,” he said in front of an unusually large media corp at the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. “Obviously, he was there from the moment I got drafted, and we had a good competitive battle. He pushed me to get better, so I’m definitely appreciative of that. And then, as far as tonight, two really great teams going at it, and there’s nothing better than that.” Still, although there’s heightened public interest in this match-up, the added emotions are nothing that he and the Celtics aren’t used to. “I’ve played a lot of playoff games, so I don’t think it’ll be that much different,” Pritchard said. Three of those games came at the very arena where the Celtics held shootaround on Tuesday morning, just a few months ago, in the first round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs Much of the discourse heading into Tuesday night will center on the dynamic between Brown and Jayson Tatum, whose relationship has been heavily scrutinized for years, especially in the last few weeks. Paul George said he expects another big night from Tatum amid all the chaos. “JT is locked in,” George said. “He’s as professional as they come at preparing for a game. He’s been playing at an MVP level, and I think he’s looking at it as another game on the schedule. Obviously, there’s a lot of noise surrounding it that hopefully he’s not lost in. But it’s our job to support him, to help him do it, and make sure his focus is where it needs to be for us to come out here and have a chance to play against a really good team and continue to add to his MVP-performance resume this season.” Pritchard was asked at shootaround what people don’t understand about NBA locker rooms, and how they differ from the locker rooms the general public is more familiar with, such as high school locker rooms. “There’s a lot of egos in it, and people need an ego to get to the NBA. And so it’s definitely a balancing act,” Pritchard said. “And in high school, like you said, it’s all your buddies. Not to say that we’re not all buddies, but everybody’s got families. They’re trying to make it. They got things to prove, so it’s different. But in the day, I don’t think there was ever beef or anything. I think it’s working relationships. Some people are closer than others, but you find a way to win and keep going.” Paul George will make his return to Philadelphia One storyline heading into Tuesday night is that Paul George will return to face the 76ers team he played for for two seasons. But there’s not too much pressure on that return game for the 9-time All-Star. “He said he’s returned to four different teams before, so he’s used to this,” he said. “So it’s nothing new to him.” George is averaging 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds, 4.1 assists, and 2.3 steals, while shooting 42.5% from three on the season. “He’s been unbelievable,” Pritchard said. “He’s played great to start the year and shooting the ball unbelievable. His defense is impeccable, so it’s been huge for us.” George said at the Celtics shootaround that he’s thoroughly enjoyed his tenure. “I’ve been kind of blown away,” he said. “I think it exceeded my expectations since being in Boston. You never know how much culture is involved and how much culture changes your outlook on things, and the effect it has mentally and physically. Just being in an environment like the culture, or like Boston presents, and so I’ve been thrilled. I’ve been playing some of my best basketball late. Just been enjoying finding out with these guys here. It’s a fun style of play. And again, I can’t talk about just the thrill and the happiness and excitement and joy that it has brought to the end of it.”

teamStories.summary: Wembanyama goes for 40 on another easy night
teamStories.detailText: PHOENIX, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 09: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs handles the ball against Oso Ighodaro #11 of the Phoenix Suns during the first half at Mortgage Matchup Center on November 09, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard not to feel like you’re watching a mirage during some of these games. The level of play is excellent and the bits and pieces you might be tempted to pick at are scarce. The wins are piling up. The vibes are good. Everything is going according to plan. Nothing to see here…right? Right! Look, I’m not going to even try to play devil’s advocate here. No one wants to be the guy pointing at the Alien dropping 40 and 11 over 25 minutes and saying, “ actually , this is bad.” If that’s a take you’d like to read then I can assure the internet is full of people willing to take you up on the offer. For my part, and if you’ve come to this website today, I’m assuring you, I genuinely find it hard to think of a less interesting angle to come at this from. Victor Wembanyama is simply brilliant. He’s been brilliant, he’s brilliant now, and he only seems to be getting more brillianter as we go along. Twelve of his fifteen made shots on Monday were dunks or layups, and nine of those were dunks. Four different teammates threw him an alley-oop. The Spurs are running a dizzying array of different motions that all end up at the same destination, which is a Wembanyama dunk. The threes, instead of feeling like something he has to do to open up the lane, now just arrive in the natural rhythm of the game. He made two threes all night, a digestif tacked on at the end of a satisfying meal. Vic even hit a Dream Shake in the middle of the 2nd quarter that left me staring off in the distance in disbelief. VICTOR WEMBANYAMA DREAM SHAKE pic.twitter.com/OF1aMWYmx4 — Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) November 10, 2026 I sometimes try to avoid writing about the Victor Wembanyama of it all when I do these because it feels too easy. What did we learn from the Spurs win? They still have the best player on the planet and he helps a lot. Case closed. To his credit, he goes out of his way to make ignoring him next to impossible. The problem, if there is one, is that regular season basketball does actually seem easy for him at this point. That’s not a mirage. I have no doubt about how hard he’s worked to achieve the level he’s currently operating on, but that doesn’t change the fact that watching him dismantle the average NBA team every other night doesn’t look very challenging. He’s like Will Hunting ranting at Professor Lambeau about how easy it is to solve those supposedly impossible graph theory equations. Victor’s ascension this season is impressive, and I want to do my best to appreciate the casual brilliance we are privy to on a regular basis, but that greatness comes at a cost, and that cost is a raised ceiling. I simply don’t care that he can drop 50 on the Mavs or 40 on the Suns. I don’t care that he can snuff out the Blazers. I’m sure there will be another jaw-dropping stat line on Wednesday when he plays the Bulls, and I’m sure it will be met with another polite nod from me. None of this is his fault, mind you. The schedule is the schedule and the teams are the teams. He’s taking care of business, and that’s all you can really ask of him. I guess I’ve just spent the last nine games of this winning streak telling myself I still don’t know what I’m looking at and I really believe anyone who tells you they do is lying. The ease with which they are winning these games is real. Every conclusion we draw from it…well, that’s a little more hazy. I try to grab on to things I know. “The Spurs are Good.” “The Suns are Bad.” “Wemby is Tall,” and project out from there but I end up feeling like I’m chasing the ghost of a conclusion. The idea of a resolution instead of an actual one. This is a champagne problem at most. Like, what, I’m having a bad time because I can’t tell if the Spurs are great, really great, or generationally amazing? A few years ago we were sitting through a sixteen-game losing streak and then an eighteen-game one, on our way to the lottery again and again. Now I’m hemming and hawing because our first brush with success last spring has got me feeling antsy. The thing I’m dancing around here is that the Finals loss is an albatross around our necks that we’re just going to have to wear. There’s no two ways about it. I’m encouraged by the things I’m seeing from this new three-guard- Hydra, but I won’t feel comfortable until I know it can outscore Jalen Brunson when he’s going Nuclear. I love that Victor seems more calm and assured in his decision making, but I still have nightmares about KAT finding a way to neutralize him. Every time we race out to a lead this season, my brain remembers the blown leads in June. The context of the past clouds everything from the present and I don’t think there’s an easy fix for that feeling. It shouldn’t sully our enjoyment of the current moment, but it does ground the results in a certain reality. All of this is certainly real enough, but none of it really matters. Not yet. Takeaways I don’t feel qualified to talk about what Dylan Harper is doing. It’s a level of basketball that I recognize as great but have difficulty quantifying, because my analysis tends to err on the side of “oh my God, how did he do that?” Nuance exits the room when he has the ball in his hands. There is a grace and fluidity to his game that is hypnotic, whether he’s getting to the basket with relative ease or casually spinning into a midrange jumper. I don’t know how to say this as a compliment, but it’s fascinatingly boring to watch. He’s operating at breakneck speed but still in complete control, sort of like how F1 cars can look a little blah during a race until you blink and realize they’re going like 200 mph. The caveat with Dylan is, obviously, his youth. It’s simultaneously the most exciting and frustrating thing about him. That control I just alluded to can prove elusive sometimes. Sometimes he seems almost like he’s just watching the game happen to him and forgets that he’s more than capable of grabbing the reins. He started the game last night a little bit adrift. Whether that’s a byproduct of the three-guard lineup’s growing pains or him simply sitting back and watching Wemby cook like the rest of us, he was kind of invisible, and a guy like Harper just shouldn’t be invisible. After the game, Mitch talked about calling him out specifically during a timeout in the 3rd, and that wake-up call seemed to snap him back into place. He absolutely torched the Suns in that 3rd quarter, going 6-of-8 from the field and effectively putting the game out of reach after Phoenix briefly tried to make a run. He is, without a doubt, the 2nd best player on the team from a talent perspective, and that this already kinda feels indisputable is the most shocking thing of all. It would’ve been so easy to just write off De’Aaron Fox this season, as evidenced by that fact that so many people did, in fact, write him off. But he’s been really fun to watch so far this year. I love the way he fits into the similar but different skill sets of our guards, and he seems a little more freed up now that Harper and Castle can take on more responsibility. He’s still so fast and he still has great vision, and last night he finished with 15 points, six assists and nine rebounds. His chemistry with Wembanyama has only gotten better, with four of those six assists going to Wemby, and their propensity for lobs and oops of all types seems to have rubbed off on everyone around them. It’s kind of exactly what you would want from a veteran leader in the starting lineup. Everyone else is right though, the Spurs probably should’ve just shipped him last summer because everyone on Twitter was mad. This pass was so stupid, lol, I love it. OMG, that Fox assist 😱 pic.twitter.com/b8cGOtJa7U — San Antonio Spurs (@spurs) November 10, 2026 WWL Postgame Press Conference Are you ever going to stop having an existential crisis about the Spurs this season? Are you kidding? My entire brand is “existential crisis about the Spurs.” What would I even write about if not that? You could analyze the gameplay? Trending stats? Maybe break down different plays the offense runs? Talk about defensive schemes? You sound insane right now. Completely bonkers. I just think people come here trying to figure out what they learned from the game and you’re only even talking about the journey through the dark night of the soul you went through on a random Monday. We’re eleven games into the season! You don’t want to, like, build to that? Shooters shoot. I’m not going to lie to the readers about the fact that I can’t sit still and watch Wembanyama dunk on dudes without stressing about the inexorable march of time or whatever. I’m not asking you to lie, but also, like, can you not sit still and just watch Wembanyama dunk on dudes without stressing about the inexorable march of time or whatever? Like, are you incapable of doing that? Is that bad? It’s not…great. Well. Yeah. He did dunk pretty good last night. He dunked very good last night.

teamStories.detailText: AUSTIN, TEXAS - APRIL 2: Musician Shakey Graves performs the Don't Mess with Texas song with dancing trashcans during a press conference at the Capitol in Austin, Tx., on Tuesday, April 02, 2013. The Texas Department of Public Safety announced a make-over for the campaign with a new look designed to appeal to those who were not born when the campaign originally launched. (Deborah Cannon/Austin American-Statesman via Getty Images) Per a Spurs press release: “The San Antonio Spurs today announced an official partnership with the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT). This new partnership will help promote TxDOT’s iconic “ Don’t mess with Texas ” campaign, which is celebrating its 40th anniversary. As a result, TxDOT will become a supporting partner of the Spurs I-35 Series, the team’s annual games in Austin.” Said Frank Miceli, chief commercial officer of Spurs Sports & Entertainment, “We take pride in calling Texas home, and caring for the communities and land around us is something we can all be part of. Together with the Don’t mess with Texas campaign, we want to turn that shared pride into everyday action by encouraging fans to keep Texas litter-free, through compelling digital and in-arena engagement. It’s a simple way to make a difference and help preserve the places we love for the next generation.” As part of the campaign, digital platforms will stream “Stories of the City,” a series dedicated to spotlighting members of the community and moments that define San Antonio. Additional promotions and activities will also be introduced at select home games. Don’t mess with Texas campaign manager Norma A. Rios added, “Spurs fans show up for their team, and we’re counting on them to show up for their state, too. We’re proud to have the Spurs on our side, reminding fans that Don’t mess with Texas means don’t litter.” Don’t mess with Texas has been educating Texans about litter prevention since 1986. Take a look at some of the past commercials that have aired over the last four decades starting with the original, Stevie Ray Vaughan: His brother, Jimmy, released an ad with his band The Fabulous Thunderbirds: NFL stars Randy White and Ed “Too Tall” Jones got in on the action: Even award-winning actor Matthew McConaughey: You can’t promote Texas without Willie Nelson. Take a look back from this news report commemorating 30 years of the classic campaign with his spot and his son recreating the classic. Over the last four decades, many iterations of the campaign have aired, showcasing just how important it is to keep Texas clear of litter. Welcome to the Thread. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. Be honest: how many of you guys had the Chicago Bears at 7-2 and in first place at the bye? There’s a long way to go, but at the midpoint of the 2026 season, the Bears look like a legit threat to win the NFC. I know it’s cliché to say, but the bye is really hitting at an opportune time for the Bears. The running back room should get a boost with D’Andre Swift able to rest up and Kyle Monangai seemingly ready to return from his toe/thumb injury. Wideout Luther Burden III, who has 49 receptions and 644 receiving yards, exited the win over the Bucs with a concussion, so he needs the break. With how much the offense has dominated the time of possession through the first nine games, the offensive line could use some relaxing time away. The Bears didn’t add anything else to the defense at the trade deadline, but the huge trade for Jeffery Simmons paid immediate dividends. He’s a force multiplier who makes everyone better. Rookie Malik Muhammad II, who has been the Bears’ best corner, should be back after the bye. Jaylon Johnson has had a rough start to the season but is coming off his best game. Kyler Gordon and Tyrique Stevenson were both dinged up on Sunday night, so a week away will do them good, and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo should be back from injured reserve soon. I also think the extra week for Caleb Williams to stew over his four-pick game will lead to an even hungrier player in the second half. The Bears are in a great place to continue their quest for back-to-back playoff appearances. How many wins will the Bears have? Are you confident in the Bears? stories.title: Reggie Wayne jokes about needing to become a player-coach after Colts trade away Josh Downs, Keenan Allen
stories.summary: Wayne played for the Colts from 2001 to 2014 and is a member of the team's Ring of Honor.
stories.detailText: The 2026 NFL trade deadline was Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. The Indianapolis Colts are 2-7 and in third place in the AFC South. Given how the season has gone so far, the Colts continued their restructuring by offloading wide receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday. Former Colts wide receiver Reggie Wayne, who has been Indy's WR coach since 2022, posted on social media after the deadline, joking that he may need to dust off his cleats and become a player-coach to help address the team's lack of depth. Welp... Might be time to dust off the old Reeboks.... 🤷🏾‍♂️ Has the player-Coach thing ever happened before? pic.twitter.com/i0CWCrPLAI — Reggie Wayne (@ReggieWayne_17) November 10, 2026 Wayne played for the Colts from 2001 to 2014. Over his career, he amassed 14,345 receiving yards and 82 touchdowns. To answer Wayne's question, yes, player-coaches have been a thing, but he is not eligible because the current Collective Bargaining Agreement bans that option. The last player-coach was Dan Reeves for the Dallas Cowboys in the early 1970s. Downs was traded to the Kansas City Chiefs along with a 2027 seventh-round pick for a 2027 fourth- and fifth-round pick. Allen went to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 sixth-round pick . The duo was Indianapolis' top two receivers this year, with Downs tallying 354 yards and a touchdown and Allen logging 351 yards and a touchdown. Without them, the Colts' wide receiver room looks like an island of misfit toys. Laquon Treadwell (215 receiving yards this year) Deion Burks (60 yards) Ashton Dulin (84 yards and 1 touchdown) Anthony Gould (16 yards) Nick Westbrook-Ikhine (0 yards) Indianapolis' current batch of wide receivers has combined for 375 yards and a touchdown so far this year. That is barely better than Downs or Allen. This new-look wide receiver room will get its first chance to prove doubters wrong on Sunday when the Colts host the Miami Dolphins.

stories.detailText: BALTIMORE, MD - JANUARY 04: Bailey Zappe #2 of the Cleveland Browns attempts a pass against the Baltimore Ravens during the first half at M&T Bank Stadium on January 4, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier on Tuesday, the Miami Dolphins announced that starting quarterback Malik Willis will be headed to the injured reserve list due to a groin injury that hampered him heavily in Week 9’s loss to the Detroit Lions. As a result, he will miss at least the next four games for the Dolphins. While Willis won’t be on the field for Miami for awhile, the team will need to bring in a new quarterback to fill out the roster. They began that process on Tuesday. The Dolphins worked out former New England Patriots and Cleveland Browns quarterback Bailey Zappe. Zappe — 27 years old — was selected in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL Draft by New England. He played in 14 games as a member of the Patriots — throwing 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions while quarterbacking the team. He joined the Browns in 2024, playing one game for the franchise. He threw one touchdown and two interceptions during that game. Most recently, Zappe was a member of the New York Jets during the offseason, but was waived by the team on cut down day. The Dolphins also worked out Austin Reed — an undrafted free agent signing of the Chicago Bears following the 2024 NFL Draft. He would start as quarterback of the Dallas Renegades in the United Football League during the 2026 season — ultimately finishing with a 4-6 record.

The Giants come into the game riding a 2-game win streak with victories over the Houston Texans and Philadelphia Eagles, which have propelled them to a 5-2-1 record on the season. The Giants are just 1.5-point favorites at home, per FanDuel. So our question this week is quick and easy: Will the Giants beat the Commanders at home on Thursday Night Football? stories.title: Giants' Nabers calls Fox analyst Olsen's body language critique a 'lie'
stories.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after the game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and being a bad teammate was a "lie."
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after Sunday's game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and the insinuation that he's a bad teammate was a "lie." Nabers was intent on speaking up for himself against some of the things said about him on the broadcast. "The thing about it is, don't tell the world something that's not me," Nabers said. "I'm speaking for myself all the time because there is nobody else that is going to be able to speak up for me. So I'm going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. "I feel like that was just a lie, attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I've never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of." The Fox broadcast showed Nabers seemingly upset during the Giants' 19-11 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles . Nabers had five catches on eight targets for 43 yards in the win, the first time since Week 3 that he has been held to fewer than 100 yards. It was Nabers' first career victory in Philadelphia and New York's first since 2013. With the Giants nursing a 13-8 lead and driving early in the fourth quarter, New York quarterback J.J. McCarthy threw behind Nabers for an incompletion, with replays later showing the receiver waving his hand and Olsen telling viewers that was a sign that Nabers wanted the ball thrown more in front of him. "His body language has been terrible today," Davis said. Olsen then quickly added: "It's just not good." There was more. The Fox crew spent several minutes throughout the broadcast talking about Nabers. In response to Nabers' post, Olsen said on social media that "at no point did we ever say he was a bad teammate." But they were critical of Nabers' body language on the sideline. The star wide receiver took offense to that, saying the audience or broadcasters didn't know what was being said on the sideline or whether he was mad or not. He intimated it was all guesswork. "My body language is the same all the time," Nabers said. "My facial expressions are the same all the time. And I think a lot of people just don't know that. They don't know me. That's OK. Just don't tell the world who I am if you don't know who I am. I felt like I just had to speak up for myself." Nabers said he hasn't spoken to Olsen since the game, but he would be open to a conversation with the former tight end. "That was two days ago, three days ago, I'm focused on the [ Washington Commanders ] game right now," Nabers said. "If he wants to reach out, he can reach out. We can have a civil conversation. But I said what I said about the situation." The Giants (5-2-1) are currently in first place in the NFC East and play the Commanders on Thursday night at MetLife Stadium. The Giants' locker room came to Nabers' defense on Tuesday. Several players told ESPN they viewed him as a "good teammate." They also see him as emotional and competitive. Running back Cam Skattebo said that Nabers needs to learn to control his emotions, but teammates and coaches also must adapt to the passion. It's especially not uncommon for wide receivers to want the football. "When you have that caliber of player that is top-three in the league, you have to understand he wants, he's demanding it, because he knows what he can do if you get him the ball. He knows what he's capable of when he has the power of the ball in his hands," Skattebo said. "And when you have a guy like that, you know, it's hard to go against them. And when he's frustrated, you understand why he's frustrated. He's not getting the ball. He's not getting the targets. And you understand that. So as a teammate, you love to see that because you know how competitive he is." Coach John Harbaugh also didn't seem to have a problem with Nabers' behavior on Sunday. He seemed to have a message for Olsen and the broadcast booth that it's probably best to avoid making judgments off body language. "I don't make too much of it because I've just been living in that world for so long and kind of understand how that goes," Harbaugh said. "As far as body language, body language is interesting. It's definitely a language, and languages are interesting because they require interpretation sometimes, especially if you don't speak the language. ... I try to stay out of all that and probably good advice for others too." Nabers is currently 11th in the NFL with 648 receiving yards in eight games despite coming off a serious knee injury. He already has four 100-yard games.

stories.title: How does ILB Daiyan Henley fit into Broncos’ long-term plans?
stories.summary: The Denver Broncos trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley was one that few of us were expecting with all eyes watching for running back news. But it was an underrated move that may pay big dividends down the road. Henley is in the final year of rookie deal, so he’ll […]
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 08: Daiyan Henley #0 of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts during the second half against the Houston against the Houston Texans at SoFi Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ryan Sun/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos trade with the Los Angeles Chargers for inside linebacker Daiyan Henley was one that few of us were expecting with all eyes watching for running back news. But it was an underrated move that may pay big dividends down the road. Henley is in the final year of rookie deal, so he’ll clearly be looking at an extension from the Broncos now that they’ve spent two picks to acquire him. Where does that leave Justin Strnad and Alex Singleton after this season? From a cap savings perspective, the green dot holding veteran Singleton would be the odd man out next March. Denver would save $4M in cap with $5M in dead money. Plus Strnad is three years younger and would incur $7M in dead money and no cap savings. The move seems to signal the teams willingness to move on from Singleton either next March or after his contract runs its course through 2027. Additionally, Henley has worn the green dot for the Chargers the last several seasons and is the leader of that defense — one that was pretty good until the whole team became a dumpster fire this season. Aside from cap and roster, Henley also fits well into the Broncos’ long-term plans through his coverage ability. This has been an annoyingly difficult area to address and this defense’s biggest weaknesses in pass defense. Coming out of college, scouting reports noted his upside and his sideline-to-sideline speed. He was considered underweight and not a great tackler. However, in the NFL that slight weight hasn’t stopped him from being the Chargers’ leading tackler every season. I think this trade is exactly what the defense needs to take things to an elite level. All that remains to be seen is how well he fits into the Vance Joseph scheme this year.
