stories.title: Commanders upgrade WR Treylon Burks to limited practice participation
stories.summary: Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams with a foot injury, but he's moving toward a return to the lineup.
stories.detailText: Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks missed last Sunday's loss to the Rams with a foot injury, but he's moving toward a return to the lineup. Burks was upgraded to limited practice participation on Tuesday. The Commanders only held a walkthrough, so that's an estimated level of work but it's still a positive sign for Burks's chances of returning against the Giants on Thursday night. Burks has 12 catches for 233 yards and two touchdowns this season. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) were listed as out for the second straight day. Head coach Dan Quinn said earlier in the day that Nick Allegretti will start at center on Thursday. Tight end John Bates (shoulder), quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow), center Matt Gulbin (knee), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hip), cornerback Amik Robertson (ankle), and defensive lineman Shy Tuttle (shoulder) were all listed as full participants.

stories.title: Malik Nabers: I felt like it was a lie for Fox broadcast to attack my character
stories.summary: "Don't tell the world something that's not me."
stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_giantsbeateagles_261109","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"577744","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_giantsbeateagles_261109","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_giantsbeateagles_261109","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"New York Giants, Philadelphia Eagles","title": "Giants are 'in control' of NFC East","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/new-york-giants-are-in-control-of-nfc-east-getting-past-philadelphia-eagles","availableDate":"2026-11-09T14:04:52Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers elaborated on his issues with comments made about him during last Sunday's Fox broadcast during a press conference on Tuesday. Fox announcers Joe Davis, Greg Olsen, and Pam Oliver discussed Nabers's body language at several points during the game and shots of an agitated Nabers on the sideline were shown multiple times. Davis was particularly critical about Nabers's response to a touchdown by teammate Isaiah Likely and Olsen said in response that "there's a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things" before adding that Nabers has "just got to keep it in check." Nabers responded to those comments and misattributed quotes that claimed Olsen called him a bad teammate in a social media post after the 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers said the broadcast tried to "create a narrative" that wasn't true and shared more thoughts on the matter Tuesday. "I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying about me," Nabers said, via a transcript from the team. "But as far as that, if it's a problem with anybody, the cameras can stay off me. The thing about it is, don't tell the world something that's not me. I'm [going to] speak up for myself all the time because there's nobody else that's going to be able to speak up for me. So, I'm going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. And I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I've never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of." Olsen took issue with the incorrect quotes about Nabers being a bad teammate and the wideout was asked if he's heard from directly from him since Sunday. Nabers said he hasn't, but "he can reach out and we can have a simple conversation." Beyond that, Nabers said he's done talking about the subject and that he's moved on to Thursday's game against the Commanders.

stories.title: Steelers had trade discussions about three WRs
stories.summary: The Steelers didn’t make a trade at the deadline, but that doesn’t mean they weren’t looking.
stories.detailText: Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers didn’t make a move ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline, but in news that should sound familiar to most fans, the team did appear to be doing its due diligence. According to Steelers insider Gerry Dulac, the Steelers had “discussions about a trade” about one of three wide receivers: the Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr., the Colts’ Josh Downs, and the Titans’ Calvin Ridley. SOURCES: Steelers had discussions about a trade for one of three WRs — Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr., Indianapolis’ Josh Downs and Tennessee’s Calvin Ridley. But Thomas and Ridley were never traded and Downs – a popular target of trade rumors – was dealt to KC. — Gerry Dulac (@gerrydulac) November 10, 2026 Downs, of course, was one of the players traded the day of the deadline, heading from Indianapolis to Kansas City with a seventh-round pick for fourth- and fifth-round selections, all in 2027. It’s worth noting the Steelers do not have a fourth-round pick in 2027. Thomas was ultimately not moved by Jacksonville, the league’s biggest buyer at the deadline, despite several months of trade rumors. Steelers beat writer Mike Kaboly reported that the Steelers were interested in Ridley, but were “soured” by the Titans wide receiver’s recent reported “incident” at Nashville International Airport . “Discussions about a trade” can mean a number of things. It’s unclear just how interested the Steelers were in adding to their wide receiver room during the season. However, Pittsburgh could be getting a reinforcement soon in Michael Pittman Jr., who Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said was “ getting close ” to a return when talking to media on Monday.

stories.title: The Rams swap out another pair of receivers following latest injury
stories.summary: The Rams lose another receiver, but bring back Xavier Smith
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams have placed another receiver on injured reserve this week, as Jordan Whittington will miss at least four games with a back injury. Whittington was in line to have serious reps moving forward with Puka Nacua joining Davante Adams on IR this week, but now that opportunity will go to someone else. Perhaps Xavier Smith, who the Rams re-signed on Tuesday in a corresponding move. Smith joins Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and C.J. Daniels in a receivers room that looks a lot different than it did a few weeks ago. LA Rams Roster Moves: • Reserved/Injured WR Jordan Whittington • Free Agent Signing WR Xavier Smith pic.twitter.com/TbAUH4OMEx — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 10, 2026 Despite rumors like that L.A. inquired about Stefon Diggs , the Rams didn’t trade for any receivers at Tuesday’s deadline. This is the group they are going with. Whittington had just four targets this season, catching two passes for 12 yards. The 22 catches for 293 yards he had as a rookie in 2024 may end up being his best career year when it’s all said and done. Instead, the Rams look to Mumpfield, last year’s seventh-round pick. This play last year has every receiver in the Rams current 11 personnel offense: Konata Mumpfield Tutu Atwell Xavier Smith There was 5 plays last year with this trio. pic.twitter.com/SY3RNYSWuU — Josh (@JoshiosTweets) November 10, 2026 Mumpfield leads all active Rams receivers with 11 catches for 162 yards. Tyler Higbee leads the team at any position among non-injured players, with 28 catches for 287 yards. Kyren Williams has 36 catches for 258 yards. Outside of a 48-yard catch against the Broncos in which Mumpfield was practically uncovered, L.A.’s new number one receiver hasn’t been productive. Aside from that play, Mumpfield has 10 catches for 114 yards and zero touchdowns in the other eight games. He had two catches for 20 yards last week. Atwell, who the team traded for at the start of the season, has been targeted nine times in the past two games, catching four passes for 68 yards. C.J. Daniels has yet to be targeted. So, the Rams bring back Xavier Smith, who had one target and no catches prior to his release. Smith had 18 catches for 303 yards in 2025, however. No News at Deadline Other notable moves on Tuesday had Josh Downs going to the Kansas City Chiefs, Keenan Allen going to the San Francisco 49ers and Brian Thomas Jr. staying with the Jasonville Jaguars . As it stands, adding Smith is the biggest move the Rams made on the NFL’s trade deadline day. Smith’s biggest moment with the Rams came in the 2025 NFC Championship game when he fumbled after halftime against the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle would go on to score a touchdown and ultimately win the game. Was that play the sole reason the Rams lost? No, but it didn’t help. Entering the 2026 season, the Rams brought Smith back as their kick returner and punt returner before waiving him a few weeks into the year . Smith then went to the 49ers, who have since traded for Allen , and decided to move on from Smith. As the Rams enter Week 10, Smith is back in L.A. McVay saw Niners got veteran Keenan Allen for a bag of chips and then said ok, time to lock in and sigh Xavier Smith https://t.co/xDpwBSYgjH — Cyborg Ninja (@thecyborglife) November 10, 2026 Is Smith the player that the Rams needed to make up for the losses of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams? Right or wrong it’s what the Rams just did, and for now, that’s all they did to address their wide receiver room as another trade deadline comes to its end.

stories.title: Rest-of-season rankings: Cousins, Jefferson, Mendoza biggest deadline winners
stories.summary: Need to make or assess a trade offer? With the NFL trade deadline passed, these rankings are designed to help.
stories.detailText: Each week, Eric Karabell ranks players by position based on their fantasy football value for the rest of the 2026 season. Use the information to optimize the players for their future potential and/or to gauge their value in trade. Eric's top 100 can be found below the positions in this column. Quarterback Rankings changes: There is movement in the top 12 as Jordan Love forces his way into the top five, C.J. Stroud returns to the top 10, and new Vikings starter Kirk Cousins gets a nice bump into QB1 range. Cousins has enjoyed a strong season, ranking fifth at QB in fantasy points, and the Vikings have a friendly schedule the rest of the way. Unlike with the Raiders, Cousins avoids losing his starting role to No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza , who also moves way up as he inherits the QB1 job. Meanwhile, Jared Goff tumbles a bit after consecutive misfires with single-digit points. Matthew Stafford lost another star receiver, which must affect his value, while Jacoby Brissett resumes starter status in a new place, Baltimore. For those in deeper leagues and superflex formats, rookies Carson Beck and Kyle McCord are starters for the Cardinals and Dolphins, respectively, as is unproven Joe Milton with the Eagles. Keep an eye on what the Colts, Chargers and perhaps Seahawks do the next few weeks as well. Running back Rankings changes: Bucky Irving continues his rise, pushing further into the top 10, while Derrick Henry continues his fall, moving more outside of it. Jonah Coleman is in the top 20, while Ashton Jeanty is barely holding onto his spot. There is much uncertainty at running back, as managers are left to guess what will happen with the Packers with Josh Jacobs (finger) out, and there is little clarity on the Patriots, Saints, Giants, Commanders and Eagles situations. Wide receiver Rankings changes: Injuries are the story here, with Puka Nacua (knee), one of the top picks in preseason drafts, out for at least the rest of the fantasy regular season and perhaps more, while promising Michael Wilson (neck) is done for the year. Learn the names Konata Mumpfield , Tutu Atwell and Reggie Virgil . Multiple Colts were traded and, naturally, individual value rises to WR4 levels -- at least -- as they head to playoff teams. Keenan Allen should see more volume with Brock Purdy and the 49ers, while Josh Downs should pile on receiving yards with Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. Justin Jefferson adds value with his QB change. Finally, rookies KC Concepcion , Jordyn Tyson and Caleb Douglas move up. Tank Dell and Mack Hollins rejoin the rankings. Tight end Rankings changes: There is no movement in the top 10. Later, Darren Waller and AJ Barner enjoyed excellent Week 9 outings, though they remain inconsistent and difficult to trust. It's time to move on from Jake Ferguson (ankle). Defense/special teams Overall top 100

stories.title: RB Jonathan Taylor, QB Daniel Jones remain with Colts as trade deadline passes
stories.summary: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor and QB Daniel Jones were the subject of trade overtures in recent days and weeks but were not traded before Tuesday's trade deadline.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- In the end, Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones are staying home. The Indianapolis Colts ' star running back and starting quarterback, respectively, were the subject of overtures by other teams in recent days and weeks but were not traded before Tuesday's trade deadline. The Colts did trade receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers , respectively. But the team's two biggest names aren't going anywhere. The Colts had been listening to trade inquiries from around the league ever since the team's slow start and subsequent firing of general manager Chris Ballard last month. That led to the trades of veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner on Oct. 27. But the Colts have long signaled the asking price for a Taylor trade was going to be high. The team, according to multiple sources, was seeking a first-round pick or equivalent compensation for the second-leading rusher in Colts history. The only team known to have come close was the New York Giants , who offered a second- and fifth-round pick, sources said. But, as Giants coach John Harbaugh confirmed Sunday, the team ultimately withdrew that offer. Whether any team made a last-minute push for the 27-year-old Taylor remains unclear. But the Colts, according to multiple sources, held firm on their position throughout the process. Still, as speculation hovered over the Colts in recent weeks, Taylor eventually expressed internally that he was open to a trade and came to terms with the notion that he might be moving on, a source told ESPN. Taylor even acknowledged the idea that last Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys might have been his last game with the Colts. "I love repping the horseshoe," Taylor said. "It's out of our control now. The hay is in the barn. Now we just play the waiting game." He added, "I think you play every game like it's your last. But at the end of the day, this has been a spot where I grew up." It's unclear what the Colts were offered for the 29-year-old Jones, but they were consistent in signaling to teams they had no intention of trading him. One team source in recent days told ESPN that the speculation surrounding a potential Jones trade should be ignored even amid the quarterback's struggles on the field. That, it appears, remained true even after the Minnesota Vikings ' quarterback woes deepened in Monday night's loss to the Buffalo Bills . The Vikings scoured the quarterback market Tuesday before finally executing a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders that reunited them with Kirk Cousins . Notably, Taylor and Jones both signed contract extensions this year. Taylor is signed through 2028 and Jones through 2027. Taylor received a $15 million signing bonus, and Jones got one for $44 million. The players are just nine games into those new deals. Another complication for the Colts is the timing. They were considering significant changes to the roster at a time when they haven't even begun in earnest the search for their next general manager. Deflecting the trade interest in Taylor and Jones means the decisions on their futures will likely fall to the team's next top executive. Some league observers told ESPN that the Colts' moves seemed inconsistent, trading some key players but holding on to two of the most valuable ones. In the end, each of the four players the Colts traded in recent weeks was in the final year of his contract and not likely to be part of the roster in 2027. Now, with eight games remaining, the Colts are ready to move past what has been a difficult few weeks. "It'll be great to get the trade deadline over," coach Shane Steichen said Monday. "There's been a lot of speculation. So, once that clears up ... we can focus on what need to focus on. And that's football." The Colts do not possess a first-round pick in 2027, but they now have 10 total selections after executing various deals. Among them is their second-round pick, two selections in the third round, three in the fourth and two in the fifth.

stories.title: Bills fill major need at safety, trade for Titans' Amani Hooker
stories.summary: The Bills traded for Titans safety Amani Hooker, giving up a second-round pick in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-round pick.
stories.detailText: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills traded for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker , giving up a second-round pick in exchange for Hooker and a fifth-round pick Tuesday. Hooker, 28, has spent his entire eight-year pro career with the Titans. He has emerged in arguably the best form of his career in 2026 in his first year in coach Robert Saleh's scheme, leading the NFL with five interceptions to go along with 52 tackles and six pass breakups. A dependable back-end option, Hooker roves between strong and free safety roles. He spent the bulk of his career as the Titans' No. 2 safety playing alongside the likes of Kevin Byard , Quandre Diggs and Xavier Woods . But the Titans consistently rewarded Hooker for his performance, extending him to new contracts in 2022 and 2025. Bills general manager Brandon Beane said discussions with Titans GM Mike Borgonzi on Hooker began about a week ago but quickly hit a wall. The Titans were still in the afterglow of the blockbuster deal to send All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago and wanted to reevaluate their unit without its leader. Talks resumed shortly after Beane and Borgonzi ran into each other at last weekend's Notre Dame-Miami college football game and truly intensified on Tuesday morning, when Beane had a lengthy chat with Titans assistant GM Dave Ziegler. Had someone asked Beane around lunchtime if he thought the Bills would come away with Hooker or any of the other defensive difference-makers they were pursuing, he would have leaned toward no. But the tenor of the conversations shifted around lunch, or rather around the time lunch would normally take place; Beane says he didn't eat this afternoon. Beane got approval on compensation from Bills owner Terry Pegula, and Borgonzi received approval from Titans controlling owner Amy Adams Strunk to strike the deal. In Hooker, Beane says the Bills landed a player who reminds him of longtime Bills safety Micah Hyde in several ways. Instincts. Ball skills. Intelligence. Steadiness. And while Beane is cautious against ever thinking of a team as "one player away," he says he favored a more aggressive approach to player acquisition this deadline in part because of the belief he has in this Bills team's connectedness and how it can lead to playoff success. Yes, Beane was aware of some of the restlessness among Bills fans hoping he'd be even more aggressive, especially after coming up empty at the trade deadline in 2025. But he emphasized how he wanted the right player, not just a player for the sake of making a deal. "I was going to make sure you guys put your guns and knives away," Beane joked with local media after the deadline. "But yeah, you don't want to just do something to do something. That's not the right way to do it, because you want to do something that makes sense for the now for this team but doesn't harm you in a terrible way for future, you know, 2027, 2028 those years." The Titans have now traded two of their defensive captains. Tennessee also sent Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chicago Bears for a 2027 first-round draft pick, a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 first-round draft pick entering Week 8. Now Hooker, who was named a defensive captain after Simmons was traded, is on his way to Buffalo. The Titans have two first-round picks and two second-round picks in next year's draft. Hooker is under contract through 2028, and his contract comes with a salary cap hit of roughly $12 million for 2026. The Bills began the season with veteran C.J. Gardner-Johnson as the answer to their safety problems, but that experiment didn't even last into the second half of the season. After signing a $6 million deal with the Bills, Gardner-Johnson underwhelmed in the early going and earned a one-game suspension for spitting at an opponent during a Week 6 matchup against Las Vegas. One day after Gardner-Johnson's suspension expired on Nov. 3, the Bills released him. Without Gardner-Johnson, the Bills' options at safety included veterans Damar Hamlin and Geno Stone as well as rookie Jalon Kilgore . Hamlin has been the primary beneficiary of Gardner-Johnson's suspension and release, starting back-to-back games next to Cole Bishop . Through six games before the bye, the Bills' secondary performed among the league's worst. Back-to-back strong performances against Baltimore and Minnesota have meant reason for hope, but those 10- and six-point showings are easier to discount given they came against overmatched backup quarterbacks Joe Fagnano and Carson Wentz . ESPN's Turron Davenport contributed to this report.

stories.title: Chargers fail to make big moves at trade deadline despite abysmal season
stories.summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers haven’t found much success during the 2026 NFL season. The trade deadline didn't help much either.
stories.detailText: Coach Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers haven’t found much success during the 2026 NFL season. The Chargers finished both the 2024 and 2025 seasons at 11-6, raising expectations that the team would be back in the playoff mix. Instead, the Chargers have lost eight straight games to start the season. General manager Joe Hortiz and the front office decided not to be an overly active participant in the trade deadline, even with trade assets on the roster such as quarterback Justin Herbert, outside linebacker Khalil Mack and receiver Ladd McConkey. ANALYSIS: NFL trade deadline winners, losers While there were expectations for the Chargers to be a potential seller at the trade deadline, the team remained quiet. If there was a chance for them to be buyers, it could have included them trying to help the offense. Harbaugh stated during his press conference on Nov. 9 that Hortiz would "be open and active in pursuing" options that would make the team better. In the hours leading up to the deadline, only one move was made and it was geared toward helping the franchise in the future. Here's what the Chargers decided to do: Chargers trade Daiyan Henley The Chargers traded linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Denver Broncos for a pair of draft picks. The Chargers now hold the rights to the Broncos' fourth-round pick in the 2027 draft and fifth-round pick in 2028. Henley was in the fourth year of his four-year rookie contract and is eligible to become a free agent ahead of the 2027 season. If Los Angeles was unable to come to terms on a potential extension, moving on from him during a lost season and acquiring draft assets serves as a good move by the organization. Chargers trade deadline grade: C- USA TODAY Sports' Jack McKessy writes : "The fourth-year linebacker's contract expires after this season, and he has struggled to adjust to new defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary's system since Jesse Minter departed for the Ravens ' head coaching job." More: Winless Chargers make first move of NFL trade deadline with AFC West partner Chargers' linebacker depth With Henley no longer on the roster, the Chargers move on with the next man up. Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax will be tasked with filling that void. The depth chart reveals that there's still a lack of depth among the inside linebackers group for the rest of the season. stories.title: From 2-7 to 6-2: Josh Downs reacts to Chiefs trade with Vince Carter GIF
stories.summary: A moment from Vince Carter's retirement ceremony helped Downs sum up his feelings about joining Kansas City.
stories.detailText: Josh Downs needed only one GIF to show how he felt about going from the 2-7 Indianapolis Colts to the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs . After Tuesday's trade , the wide receiver posted a popular clip of Vince Carter overcome with emotion during his Toronto Raptors jersey retirement ceremony. Often used to celebrate good news, the GIF presumably represented Downs' feelings about his new destination. The moment dates to Nov. 2, 2024, when Carter became the first player to have his jersey retired by the Raptors . His emotional reaction as Toronto honored his No. 15 has since taken on a life of its own online. Downs' post also caught the attention of his new quarterback, Patrick Mahomes , who reposted it with a clock emoji. Downs, who had requested a trade, heads to Kansas City with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for fourth- and fifth-round selections. He brings 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown this season to a Chiefs receiver group dealing with injuries to Tyquan Thornton and Xavier Worthy . The GIF wasn't Downs' only message Tuesday. He also thanked the team that drafted him in the third round in 2023. "I am beyond grateful and blessed for my time in Indy. Nothing but love For the Shoe," he wrote on X.

stories.title: 32 grades on the 2026 NFL trade deadline: Who won, who lost and who did nothing?
stories.summary: Once we accept the 4-5 Raiders weren't a real playoff contender this season, the Kirk Cousins trade is brilliant. As for the Colts, no Jonathan Taylor trade? What's the point in keeping him?
stories.detailText: The NFL trade deadline went down at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Here's a breakdown of the trades and grades. Yahoo Sports' Eric Edholm assessed the NFC teams and Frank Schwab tackled the AFC. Trade activity is noted from late August: NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers Dallas Cowboys Trade deadline activity In CB Joey Porter Jr. (from Steelers, Oct. 1) OL Broderick Jones (from Steelers, Aug. 29) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from Steelers, part of Jones deal on Aug. 29) Out 2027 third-round draft pick (to Steelers, part of Jones deal on Aug. 29) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Steelers, part of Jones deal on Aug. 29) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Steelers, part of Porter deal on Oct. 1) 2028 second-round draft pick (to Steelers, part of Porter deal on Oct. 1) The Cowboys' big move came on Oct. 1 when they traded for CB Joey Porter Jr. for multiple picks. Looking back now, the move looks good from a value standpoint, as Jessie Bates III ended up being traded for more, and Porter has played pretty well for Dallas. The problem is that Porter has played in only four of Dallas' six games, and the Cowboys are still treading water. Team owner Jerry Jones hinted that the Cowboys were still big-game hunting in the trade market, but nothing else emerged. Trade deadline grade: B- New York Giants Trade deadline activity In QB J.J. McCarthy (from Vikings, Sept. 28) Out 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Vikings, part of McCarthy deal on Sept. 28) The Giants have had a fascinating pre-deadline period, acquiring J.J. McCarthy for nickels on the dollar and potentially changing the team's landscape at the position. Jaxson Dart presumably remains the 2027 starter, but a strong finish from McCarthy could set up some interesting optics next offseason. They were sellers before the draft, trading Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati, but the Giants were shopping right up until the deadline as NFC East leaders. They reportedly went in hard on Jeffery Simmons and made the Colts a strong offer on Jonathan Taylor, but nothing materialized. Trade deadline grade: B- Philadelphia Eagles Trade deadline activity In 2027 fifth-round draft pick (from Ravens, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) 2028 second-round draft pick (from Ravens, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) 2027 first-round pick (from Jaguars, part of Jordan Davis deal on Nov. 9) 2029 second-round pick (from Jaguars, part of Jordan Davis deal on Nov. 9) Out C Cam Jurgens (to Ravens, Oct. 7) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Ravens, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) DT Jordan Davis (to Jaguars, Nov. 9) It has been a surprising turn of events with the Eagles — often among the more aggressive teams around deadline time — turning into sellers. Philadelphia dealt A.J. Brown this offseason but also traded for multiple players, so that felt like a separate situation. The in-season loss of Jalen Hurts has precipitated some of this movement, but the Eagles were already in sell mode with the Cam Jurgens trade the week prior to Hurts being diagnosed with blood clots. Trading Davis brought back some potentially great returns. It's not how we imagined it going, but the Eagles were smart to pivot, especially Hurts' murky future. Trade deadline grade: B+ Washington Commanders Trade deadline activity No trade deadline activity The Commanders were reportedly open to the idea of trading DT Daron Payne, whose contract expires after this season, but he suffered a broken foot, thus killing off any deal. The same might have been true for Javon Kinlaw, who is also on IR. The team's salary cap situation is fine, but the Commanders are underwater at 2-5-1 and could use the draft-pick help. They've made only 11 selections combined the past two drafts, with a roster that needs an influx of young talent. Trade deadline grade: C- Chicago Bears Trade deadline activity In DT Jeffery Simmons (from Titans, Oct. 29) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (from Titans, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) Out 2027 first-round draft pick (to Titans, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) 2028 first-round draft pick (to Titans, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (to Titans, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) It's possible we look back at the Simmons trade as the most impactful of the 2026 cycle. In Simmons' first game as a Bear, he took over against the Seahawks, giving the team and its fans hope for another Super Bowl run. Two first-round picks is potentially a significant cost for a defensive tackle, but if the Bears finish closer to the top of the standings, those picks might be worth about the same as the No.10 overall selection the Bengals paid for Dexter Lawrence. The Simmons trade was aggressive and could help put the Bears over the top. What's not to like? Trade deadline grade: A Detroit Lions Trade deadline activity In S Andre Cisco (from Jets, Nov. 9) Out 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Jets, part of Andre Cisco deal on Nov. 9) Lions The Lions were reportedly one of the first teams to inquire about Joey Porter Jr., and when he went to Dallas, Lions fans were not too happy with general manager Brad Holmes. The Lions have added safety depth, acquiring Cisco from the Jets. Their defensive concerns likely remain, even with stronger play of late, but Holmes resisted making any big moves. Trade deadline grade: C Green Bay Packers Trade deadline activity RB Kaleb Johnson (from Steelers, Aug. 30) TE Mark Redman (from Rams, Aug. 30) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Dolphins, part of Kyle McCord deal on Aug. 30) Out QB Kyle McCord (to Dolphins, Aug. 30) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Steelers, part of Kaleb Johnson deal on Aug. 30) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (to Rams, part of Mark Redman deal on Aug. 30) The Packers started the season 1-2 but have ripped off five wins in their past six games and are emerging as a sneaky title contender, especially with Micah Parsons on his way back. That likely will have to count Green Bay's big "acquisition" this season, although they did reportedly kick the tires on Jonathan Taylor amid Josh Jacobs' once-uncertain status. Do the Packers have enough to make a big run? We'll find out. Trade deadline grade: C Minnesota Vikings In 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Patriots, part of Walter Rouse deal on Aug. 30) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (from Giants, part of J.J. McCarthy deal on Sept. 28) QB Kirk Cousins (from Raiders, Nov. 10) Out OT Walter Rouse (to Patriots, Aug. 30) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Patriots, part of Walter Rouse deal on Aug. 30) QB J.J. McCarthy (to Giants, Sept. 28) 2027 third-round draft pick (to Raiders, part of Cousins deal on Nov. 10) The Vikings shipped out McCarthy to the Giants, and it seemed to backfire initially with McCarthy showing early promise in New York and Carson Wentz struggling against the Bills in place of an injured Kyler Murray. That prompted the Vikings to bring Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota, where he played for head coach Kevin O'Connell previously, in a desperate attempt to provide offensive stability. The Vikings have a world-class defense, and it would be criminal not to give that unit a fighting chance to compete for a Super Bowl. We'll see how quickly Cousins can re-integrate into the system, but a third-round pick likely means they're serious about him starting quickly. Trade deadline grade: C+ Atlanta Falcons In DT Gervon Dexter Sr. (from Bears, Aug. 30) 2027 second-round draft pick (from Jaguars, part of Jessie Bates III deal on Nov. 9) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (from Jaguars, part of Jessie Bates III deal on Nov. 9) G Andrew Vorhees (from Ravens, Nov. 10) sixth-round draft pick (from Ravens, part of Ryan Neuzil deal on Nov. 10) Out CB Clark Phillips III (to Bears, Aug. 30) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Bears, part of Gervon Dexter Sr. deal on Aug. 30) S Jessie Bates III (to Jaguars, Nov. 9) C Ryan Neuzil (to Ravens, Nov. 10) You can say the Falcons were technically in a divisional playoff race when they dumped Jessie Bates III for draft picks. On the other hand, you can also reasonably understand the thinking of the trade when you consider the terrific value Atlanta received and also that the Falcons likely were more fool's-gold contenders. They'll have a good allotment of draft picks heading into what should be a significant offseason for the franchise. Trade deadline grade: B+ Carolina Panthers In DT TeRah Edwards (from Chargers, Aug. 30) Out 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Chargers, part of TeRah Edwards deal on Aug. 30) The Panthers spent big on two defensive pieces this offseason, signing Jaelan Phillips and Devin Lloyd for big money, and they've mostly rested on their laurels since. The results have been underwhelming, and Carolina sits at 3-5. That's miraculously tied for first place. The Panthers are contenders, but they're not overextending themselves for a big run at the NFC South crown. Trade deadline grade: C New Orleans Saints In 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Jaguars, part of Davon Godchaux deal on Nov. 9); could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick Out DT Davon Godchaux (to Jaguars, Nov. 9) The Saints' first pre-deadline move was to ship out Godchaux to the Jaguars for a future Day 3 pick. It was not the kind of inspiring move some fans hoped for after a dramatic win over the Browns, keeping the Saints in the divisional hunt. Realistically, the Saints were always more likely to be sellers than buyers, with limited upside this season. Trade deadline grade: C+ Tampa Bay Buccaneers No trade deadline activity Like most NFC South teams, the Buccaneers had been more connected to selling than buying. Vita Vea's name popped up in some trade rumors in the past week, with the Giants reportedly among the teams interested, but nothing materialized after Vea signed a one-year, $30 million extension in August. And despite the Bucs needing some skill-position help on offense, they apparently were willing to wait until the offseason for any major additions. Trade deadline grade: C Arizona Cardinals In TE Hunter Long (from Jaguars, Aug. 30) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Jaguars, part of Hunter Long deal on Aug. 30) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Patriots, part of Corey Kiner deal on Aug. 29) 2027 second-round draft pick (from Texans, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from Texans, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from Ravens, part of Jacoby Brissett deal on Nov. 4) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Ravens, part of Jacoby Brissett deal on Nov. 4) Out RB Corey Kiner (to Patriots, Aug. 29) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Jaguars, part of Hunter Long deal on Aug. 30) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (to Texans, Oct. 12) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Texans, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) QB Jacoby Brissett (to Ravens, Nov. 4) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Ravens, part of Jacoby Brissett deal on Nov. 4) The Cardinals sent Harrison to the Texans back on Oct. 11 in a move that all but admitted defeat on the pick. Since the trade, Harrison has caught six passes for 60 yards and a score, so perhaps Arizona did well getting what it could for a depreciating asset. The Jacoby Brissett trade was a no-brainer; there was no real reason to keep him around, getting two picks in return. This is a multi-year rebuild for a team still seeking several franchise pillars, so it's smart to continue stacking resources for the offseason without dealing off players such as Trey McBride. Trade deadline grade: B Los Angeles Rams In WR Tutu Atwell (from Dolphins, Aug. 27) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Packers, part of Mark Redman deal on Aug. 30) Out RB Jarquez Hunter (to Dolphins, Aug. 27) TE Mark Redman (to Packers, Aug. 30) The Rams stood pat at the deadline despite losing starting receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua to injuries. One reason is that the Rams made two major trades this offseason, landing Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie. Their pick allotment has been seriously dented over the next three draft cycles. Another reason to be quiet at the deadline: money. The Rams are cap-strapped, sitting right at the mark, with little or no realistic flexibility. They may have wanted to do something dramatic to help turn around their Super Bowl-hopeful season, but the Rams will have to roll mostly with what they have. Trade deadline grade: C San Francisco 49ers In OL Jarrett Patterson (from Texans, Aug. 30) DT DeForest Buckner (from Colts, Oct. 27) Out 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Texans, part of Jarrett Patterson deal on Aug. 30) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (to Colts, part of DeForest Buckner deal on Oct. 27) Bringing DeForest Buckner back felt like a smart move, filling a thin position and giving the Niners a familiar face in the locker room at the cost of a Day 3 pick. They'll still need to re-sign Buckner to get better value from the trade, but that feels entirely likely at this point. Even with the health forecast at receiver appearing to be improve, the Niners also picked up Keenan Allen, who can be quality Mike Evans insurance. The secondary was one spot they could have upgraded, with Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir both injured in Week 9, but they opted to stand pat there. Trade deadline grade: B Seattle Seahawks In CB Avery Smith (from Chargers, Aug. 30) G Quenton Nelson (from Colts, Oct. 27) Out 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Chargers, part of Avery Smith deal on Aug. 30) 2027 third-round draft pick (to Colts, part of Quenton Nelson deal on Oct. 27) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (to Colts, part of Quenton Nelson deal on Oct. 27) The Quenton Nelson trade was a big swing, but it came with bad luck when it was discovered after his first game that he needed a minor, in-season knee procedure. It's not expected to keep Nelson down for too long, with the Seahawks not expected to place him on injured reserve, but it hurts them in the short term. They paid a good price for Nelson, who's a free agent next spring, and the Seahawks presumably would like to re-sign him if his knee is good. Trade deadline grade: C+ Buffalo Bills In 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Colts, part of Sedrick Van Pran-Granger deal on Aug. 30) S Amani Hooker (from Titans, Nov. 10) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (from Titans, part of Amani Hooker deal on Nov. 10) Out C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (to Colts, Aug. 30) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Colts, part of Sedrick Van Pran-Granger deal on Aug. 30) 2027 second-round draft pick (to Titans, part of Hooker deal on Nov. 10) The Bills had been watching other contenders make moves before the trade deadline, and knew they had to do something. They made a fairly big move for safety Amani Hooker, who was having a very good season for the Titans. The Bills defense has looked better lately, but that came against terrible quarterback play. Buffalo cut problematic safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson a few weeks ago and needed a replacement, and came up with an upgrade. Trade deadline grade: B+ Miami Dolphins In RB Jarquez Hunter (from Rams, Aug. 27) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Jaguars, part of Quinn Ewers deal on Aug. 29) QB Kyle McCord (from Packers, Aug. 30) Out WR Tutu Atwell (to Rams, Aug. 27) QB Quinn Ewers (to Jaguars, Aug. 29) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Packers, part of Kyle McCord deal on Aug. 30) The Dolphins didn't have many trade assets, but they did have a few. Offensive tackle Austin Jackson and defensive tackle Zach Sieler could have been moved but weren't. Sieler in particular seemed obvious to move, as he's 31 on a team in a long-term rebuild. The Dolphins could have used some picks for him. Trade deadline grade: D+ New England Patriots In S Jaylen Reed (from Texans, Aug. 24) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Texans, part of Kayshon Boutte deal on Aug. 24) RB Corey Kiner (from Cardinals, Aug. 29) OL Walter Rouse (from Vikings, Aug. 30) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from Vikings, part of Walter Rouse deal on Aug. 30) Out WR Kayshon Boutte (to Texans, Aug. 24) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (to Cardinals, part of Corey Kiner deal on Aug. 29) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Vikings, part of Walter Rouse deal on Aug. 30) The Patriots were surprisingly quiet before the deadline. Running back seemed like a big need with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson dealing with injuries. Interior offensive line could have used some help too. It's not egregious for the Patriots to not make a trade, but it could have helped. Trade deadline grade: C- New York Jets In OL Jordan Meredith (from Raiders, Aug. 30) 2029 seventh-round draft pick (from Raiders, part of Jordan Meredith deal on Aug. 30) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Lions, part of Andre Cisco deal on Nov. 9) Out 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Raiders, part of Jordan Meredith deal on Aug. 30) S Andre Cisco (to Lions, Nov. 9) The Jets' big move was shipping safety Andre Cisco to the Lions for a sixth-round pick. And really, that's fine. Most of the Jets' big trade pieces were young players they should want to hold onto. They made big moves last season before the deadline to stockpile picks, so there was no need to be in the mix this year. Trade deadline grade: C+ Baltimore Ravens In 2028 seventh-round draft pick (from Giants, part of CJ Okoye deal on Aug. 29) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Chiefs, part of Diego Pounds deal on Aug. 29) C Cam Jurgens (from Eagles, Oct. 7) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from Eagles, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) QB Jacoby Brissett (from Cardinals, Nov. 4) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (from Cardinals, part of Jacoby Brissett deal on Nov. 4) C Ryan Neuzil (from Falcons, Nov. 10) G Andrew Vorhees (to Falcons, Nov. 10) sixth-round draft pick (to Falcons, part of Ryan Neuzil deal on Nov. 10) Out DL CJ Okoye (to Giants, Aug. 29) OL Diego Pounds (to Chiefs, Aug. 29) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Eagles, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) 2028 second-round draft pick (to Eagles, part of Cam Jurgens deal on Oct. 7) The Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett just to have some hope on offense. There was none with Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on IR. It was a little surprising to see a fourth-round pick involved, though Baltimore got a fifth-round pick back. But that move without any follow-up is a bit odd: Brissett isn't going to save the season, there was nothing else added to help out but yet the Ravens traded picks to be … what exactly? The Ravens got center Cam Jurgens weeks ago, but that came at the hefty price of a second-round pick to Philadelphia. Trade deadline grade: C- Cincinnati Bengals No activity The Bengals made their big trade in the offseason when they sent a first-round pick to the Giants for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II. That trade had a profound impact on the defense, but doesn't count for this grade. It would have been nice to see the Bengals make more additions before the deadline, especially with Joe Burrow playing at an MVP level. Trade deadline grade: D Cleveland Browns No activity The one move that could have and probably should have happened was trading receiver Jerry Jeudy. Maybe there wasn't much of a market for him, but he's also not making a big impact for a Browns team that is turning to its young rookie receivers. Not making any moves is fine though a Jeudy trade would have been wise. Trade deadline grade: C Pittsburgh Steelers In 2027 third-round draft pick (from Cowboys, part of Broderick Jones deal on Aug. 29) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Cowboys, part of Broderick Jones deal on Aug. 29) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Packers, part of Kaleb Johnson deal on Aug. 30) 2028 second-round draft pick (from Cowboys, part of Joey Porter Jr. deal on Oct. 1) 2027 sixth-round draft pick, conditional (from Cowboys, part of Joey Porter Jr. deal on Oct. 1) Out OT Broderick Jones (to Cowboys, Aug. 29) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (to Cowboys, part of Broderick Jones deal on Aug. 29) RB Kaleb Johnson (to Packers, Aug. 30) CB Joey Porter Jr. (to Cowboys, Oct. 1) The Steelers simply had enough with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and traded him to the Cowboys for a second- and sixth-round pick, which was a nice return for a player who was becoming a distraction. Trade deadline grade: C Houston Texans In WR Kayshon Boutte (from Patriots, Aug. 24) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from 49ers, part of Jarrett Patterson deal on Aug. 30) OT Nathan Thomas (from Cowboys, Aug. 30) WR Marvin Harrison Jr. (from Cardinals, Oct. 12) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Cardinals, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) Out S Jaylen Reed (to Patriots, Aug. 24) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (to Patriots, part of Kayshon Boutte deal on Aug. 24) OL Jarrett Patterson (to 49ers, Aug. 30) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Cowboys, part of Nathan Thomas deal on Aug. 30) 2027 second-round draft pick (to Cardinals, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Cardinals, part of Marvin Harrison Jr. deal on Oct. 12) Getting Marvin Harrison Jr., and giving up a second-round pick, seemed like a steep price for a receiver who has been a big disappointment in the NFL. He has six catches for 60 yards in three games, and that's the type of production that can be found off someone's practice squad. Trade deadline grade: D Indianapolis Colts In C Sedrick Van Pran-Granger (from Bills, Aug. 30) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from Bills, part of Sedrick Van Pran-Granger deal on Aug. 30) 2027 third-round draft pick (from Seahawks, part of Quenton Nelson deal on Oct. 27) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (from Seahawks, part of Quenton Nelson deal on Oct. 27) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from 49ers, part of DeForest Buckner deal on Oct. 27) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from Chiefs, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (from Chiefs, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from 49ers, part of Keenan Allen deal on Nov. 10) Out 2027 sixth-round draft pick (to Bills, part of Sedrick Van Pran-Granger deal on Aug. 30) G Quenton Nelson (to Seahawks, Oct. 27) DT DeForest Buckner (to 49ers, Oct. 27) WR Josh Downs (to Chiefs, Nov. 10) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (to Chiefs, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) WR Keenan Allen (to 49ers, Nov. 10) The Colts started early, trading defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and guard Quenton Nelson for third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks. They also got a sixth for veteran Keenan Allen, which was smart. Moving Josh Downs for fourth- and fifth-round picks was fine too. But no Jonathan Taylor trade? What's the point in keeping him? Daniel Jones was never going to be moved, but Taylor should have been. Trading all those players and not even getting a single first- or second-round pick is a bit disappointing. Trade deadline grade: B- Jacksonville Jaguars In QB Quinn Ewers (from Dolphins, Aug. 29) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Cardinals, part of Hunter Long deal on Aug. 30) S Jessie Bates III (from Falcons, Nov. 9) DT Davon Godchaux (from Saints, Nov. 9) DT Jordan Davis (from Eagles, Nov. 9) Out 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Dolphins, part of Quinn Ewers deal on Aug. 29) TE Hunter Long (to Cardinals, Aug. 30) 2028 seventh-round draft pick (to Cardinals, part of Hunter Long deal on Aug. 30) 2027 second-round draft pick (to Falcons, part of Jessie Bates III deal on Nov. 9) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (to Falcons, part of Jessie Bates III deal on Nov. 9) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (to Saints, part of Davon Godchaux deal on Nov. 9); could elevate to a 2027 sixth-round pick 2027 first-round pick (to Eagles, part of Jordan Davis deal on Nov. 9) 2029 second-round pick (to Eagles, part of Jordan Davis deal on Nov. 9) We can't ignore the cost involved with the Jaguars' series of trades. They traded away a first-round pick, two seconds, a fifth and a sixth. But the mission is clear: Safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux are coming to help the Jaguars make their first Super Bowl. You have to admire the courage to be aggressive and chase a title. Trade deadline grade: A- Tennessee Titans In 2027 first-round draft pick (from Bears, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) 2028 first-round draft pick (from Bears, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from Bears, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) 2027 second-round draft pick (from Bills, part of Amani Hooker deal on Nov. 10) Out DT Jeffery Simmons (to Bears, Oct. 29) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (to Bears, part of Jeffery Simmons deal on Oct. 29) S Amani Hooker (to Bills, Nov. 10) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Bills, part of Amani Hooker deal on Nov. 10) It hurts to trade Jeffery Simmons away. He was a great player for the Titans. But the reality for Tennessee is it's a one-win team and Simmons is 29 years old. Simmons might not still be great when the Titans start to turn the corner. To get two first-round picks back for Simmons was good business for a rebuilding team. It was also great to turn a hot start from safety Amani Hooker (and a fifth-round pick) into a second-round draft pick from the Bills. Trade deadline grade: A Denver Broncos In LB Daiyan Henley (from Chargers, Nov. 10) Out 2027 fourth-round draft pick (to Chargers, part of Daiyan Henley deal on Nov. 10) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (to Chargers, part of Daiyan Henley deal on Nov. 10) It seemed like the Broncos offense needed some help, but the defense got the boost. The Broncos got linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Chargers for a fourth- and fifth-round pick, which was a nice deal. Defense didn't seem like an obvious need but Henley is now Denver's best coverage linebacker, which was an area of weakness. There are still questions on offense that weren't addressed, but getting Henley was still a plus. Trade deadline grade: B Kansas City Chiefs In OL Joshua Ezeudu (from Giants, Aug. 26) OT Diego Pounds (from Ravens, Aug. 29) WR Josh Downs (from Colts, Nov. 10) 2027 seventh-round draft pick (from Colts, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) Out 2028 seventh-round draft pick (to Giants, part of Joshua Ezeudu deal on Aug. 26) 2028 sixth-round draft pick, conditional (to Ravens, part of Diego Pounds deal on Aug. 29) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (to Colts, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) 2027 fifth-round draft pick (to Colts, part of Josh Downs deal on Nov. 10) The Chiefs needed some receiving help and Josh Downs has always been a player who should have been more productive in Indianapolis. Now the Chiefs have a chance to unlock his potential. The cost of a fourth- and fifth-round pick (with a seventh coming back to Kansas City) wasn't trivial but it was a worthwhile gamble. Trade deadline grade: B Las Vegas Raiders In 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Jets, part of Jordan Meredith deal on Aug. 30) 2027 third-round draft pick (from Vikings, part of Kirk Cousins deal on Nov. 10) Out OL Jordan Meredith (to Jets, Aug. 30) 2029 seventh-round draft pick (to Jets, part of Jordan Meredith deal on Aug. 30) QB Kirk Cousins (to Vikings, Nov. 10) Once we accept the 4-5 Raiders weren't a real playoff contender this season, the Kirk Cousins trade is brilliant. Cousins was going to start perhaps a few more games before the team shifted to Fernando Mendoza. But they flipped a half-season of Cousins into a third-round pick from the Vikings. That's not a move most teams who aren't completely dead in the playoff race would make. It was perfect for the Raiders. Trade deadline grade: A Los Angeles Chargers In 2027 sixth-round draft pick (from Seahawks, part of Avery Smith deal on Aug. 30) 2028 sixth-round draft pick (from Panthers, part of TeRah Edwards deal on Aug. 30) 2027 fourth-round draft pick (from Broncos, part of Daiyan Henley deal on Nov. 10) 2028 fifth-round draft pick (from Broncos, part of Daiyan Henley deal on Nov. 10) Out CB Avery Smith (to Seahawks, Aug. 30) DT TeRah Edwards (to Panthers, Aug. 30) LB Daiyan Henley (to Broncos, Nov. 10) Teams don't often trade within the division, so it was surprising to see the Chargers trade linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos. He's just 26 years old, though he is on the final year of his rookie deal and due a big pay raise. The Chargers got a good 2027 pick and a 2028 fifth, but that still seems light for a good, young player. And not trading Khalil Mack is simply befuddling. Trade deadline grade: D

stories.title: Commanders injury report: Treylon Burks, Chig Okonkwo make strides
stories.summary: Commanders receiver Treylon Burks was limited during the most important practice heading into the Giants clash.
stories.detailText: Treylon Burks had a big Tuesday ahead. He needed to work and show the Commanders that he can play again. This was a big practice, and, honestly, the only one where the veteran receiver could prove worthy of playing in Thursday’s game against the New York Giants. Are we sure he’s going to go? We are not. But there’s some hope after he was considered limited on the Commanders’ official injury report. Tight end Colson Yankoff was a DNP for the second straight day with a knee injury, putting his availability in a tough spot. Head coach Dan Quinn also made it clear in his Tuesday press conference that center Lucas Patrick is in the concussion protocol and won’t play against the Giants. He clearly stated that Nick Allegretti will start in his place. In a positive development, tight end Chig Okonkwo was a full participant on Tuesday. stories.title: Does 49ers trade for Keenan Allen solidify their Super Bowl hopes?
stories.summary: The San Francisco 49ers traded for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen before the NFL deadline. Does he help tip the Niners Super Bowl odds?
stories.detailText: The San Francisco 49ers acquired veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 sixth-round pick just hours before the NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10. It's no secret around the NFL that the Niners have a shortage of available wideouts, making the addition of Allen all the more vital to San Francisco's passing game. The 49ers have been dealt injuries throughout the season Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and Christian Kirk. Each week, there has been someone in the Niners' WR room who steps up to the mantle. Now, Allen gets his turn as San Francisco found their plug-in at receiver. He returns to the Bay Area having played his collegiate years at Cal from 2010 to 2012. From Cal, he was selected by San Diego Chargers with the 76th overall pick in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. Allen was runner-up for Offensive Rookie of the Year but he developed into the Chargers' No. 1-receiver. He would become a six-time Pro Bowl selection in 10 seasons, even as the team moved to Los Angeles. He spent a season with the Chicago Bears in 2024, then returned to LA for another season with the Chargers. He signed with Indianapolis during the offseason. With Allen back on the West Coast, the hope is to earn the league's most prized piece of jewelry. Does Allen have enough left in the tank to help bring a Super Bowl to the Bay Area? How does Keenan Allen fit in with 49ers at WR? Allen comes to San Francisco as a 34-year-old veteran receiver in his 14th NFL season, which bears the question of if he has enough in the tank to be a contributing piece to the 49ers offense. Allen is added to a star-studded wide receiver room, but still, looming injuries loom are a cause of concern, at least until guys start trending upward. He'll likely come in as a starter. Allen is known for his elite route-running, high IQ and superb ball-tracking and catching ability. Nothing thrown Allen's way gets dropped. Allen caught 40 balls for 351 yards and 1 touchdown in eight games with the Colts during the 2026 NFL season. He's shared 22% of targets and has a nearly 69% catch rating. He averages 8.8 yards per catch. His addition provides Brock Purdy with another weapon to find trust in, especially while the San Francisco receiver room slowly gets healthy. Adding Allen means the team doesn't necessarily have to rush guys back to the field. Plus, Jordan Watkins is coming off a week where he caught four passes for 86 yards and a touchdown. He continues to improve. Having a threat like Allen alongside Watkins will likely open things up for himself. Can Keenan Allen help 49ers to a Super Bowl title? The 49ers are still the favorite to win the Super Bowl with +550 odds, according to BetMGM , currently tied with the Buffalo Bills. For San Francisco, the team's hopes will ride on health and availability. Allen isn't a young buck anymore at 34. Example A, Evans is 33 years old and look how much time he's missed. No question at what the 49ers will get from the vets on the field, it's a matter of getting them on the field at 100%. Allen has been relatively healthy in 2026 and that's good news for San Francisco. Allen appeared in every game, except one, for the Colts having missed Week 4 with a groin injury. Since then, he's been dependable, especially production wise. Maybe not the fantasy pickup he once was, but Allen does the things that contributes to winning football games. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Does 49ers trade for Keenan Allen solidify their Super Bowl hopes?

stories.title: Grading the trade: Josh Downs gives Chiefs WR help they needed, but is he the right fit?
stories.summary: Although Downs isn't a true deep threat, he should give the Chiefs a badly needed threat from the slot.
stories.detailText: Just prior to the trade deadline, the Kansas City Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. The Chiefs will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick, and the Colts will get back fourth- and fifth-round picks in 2027. Downs, 25, who recently requested a trade, got his wish and now will team up with Patrick Mahomes. In nine games (seven starts) with the Colts this season, Downs caught 33 passes for 354 yards and one TD on 57 targets. Downs also had a team-high seven catches for 72 yards on nine targets in the Colts’ 33-30 loss in Kansas City back in Week 2. Who won this trade? Let’s dive into the debate. Chiefs address obvious WR need, even if it’s not a perfect fit The Chiefs were in big need of adding receiver help. Not one wideout on the roster has either 50 targets or 300 yards receiving on the season. Downs, sharing the lead role in Indy along with Keenan Allen (and with Alec Pierce hurt), has surpassed both marks. That’s not to say that he instantly will become Patrick Mahomes’ go-to target. But it’s hard not to imagine Downs stepping in and earning a fairly sizable role in Kansas City’s offense, assuming he can develop a relationship with Mahomes and pick up the playbook quickly. Downs has primarily been a slot receiver in his career, although his work rate playing outside has increased slightly in 2026 out of need. It would make sense to put him in the slot, although what makes him, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy attractive is that they can line up in multiple spots. Rice’s numbers over the past year-plus have been slightly better inside, but Worthy has been far more efficient as a perimeter receiver in his career. That likely means Downs can take those snaps and do what he does best: run efficient routes, separate quickly and generate first downs. The biggest drawback is that Downs is not a deep threat, which was probably their biggest need. This move also can help the Chiefs’ punt-return situation. Nikko Remigio has struggled in that role this season. Downs has only returned two punts this season, but he has a very respectable 9.8-yard career average on punt returns. The Chiefs know that Downs is a free agent after the season, and they had to be comfortable with the idea of this trade potentially being a half-season rental. Thinning out their Day 3 pick allotment stings a little, but the price wasn’t that steep in the big picture, especially when you compare it to what the Seahawks paid for Rashid Shaheed (fourth- and fifth-round picks) and what the Jaguars dealt for Jakobi Meyers (fourth- and sixth-rounders) before last year’s deadline. This move is about taking advantage of a championship window with Mahomes showing he’s recovered from his knee injury and Travis Kelce still performing at a relatively high level in his expected swan-song season. Grade : B+ Colts continue teardown with an expected trade Downs requested a trade and got his wish. The Colts likely weren’t convinced they had to extend him, and Downs probably wasn’t returning to Indianapolis next season anyway, so trading him now made perfect sense instead of waiting for compensatory-pick returns more than a year from now. It fits right in line with the other trades they’ve made since firing GM Chris Ballard, shipping out one-time franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and also dealing Allen. When you consider what they got back for Downs, which was two early Day 3 picks, it was a pretty fair market price. Not having a first-rounder next spring from the Sauce Gardner will continue to sting. But with the trades, they’ve managed to replenish the cupboard a bit. They already have seven Day 3 picks to work with and are projected to receive two more compensatory selections in that same range. Having those picks can allow the Colts potentially to slide up in the draft, and quarterback could be on the menu given the uncertainty surrounding Daniel Jones, even if Jones was not traded by the deadline. They’ll also eventually need to replenish a gutted WR room, but for now the Colts can see what they have in the likes of Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin, Deion Burks, Laquon Treadwell and, of course, Pierce, when he’s back healthy again. It wouldn’t be stunning if the Colts only bring back a few of these players next year, but the remainder of the season will help them decide who stays and who goes. Grade : B

stories.title: Falcons steal K Jake Moody from Ravens’ practice squad
stories.summary: The Ravens are once again looking for a new kicker with Tyler Loop on IR and Jake Moody headed to Atlanta.
stories.detailText: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 05: Jake Moody #45 of the Baltimore Ravens kicks a 53 yard field goal against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the first quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 05, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens need a new kicker. Again. The Atlanta Falcons are signing Jake Moody off of the Ravens’ practice squad, per NFL insider Jordan Schultz , robbing Baltimore of another kicker less than a week after Week 1 starter Tyler Loop landed on injured reserve with a groin injury. The move raises questions about the Ravens’ approach to their kicker situation with Loop sidelined for at least four games. The team had a roster spot available, but opted to elevate Moody from the practice squad to face the Jacksonville Jaguars last Thursday. With only two elevations remaining, he would have required a promotion to the 53-man roster to see out Loop’s absence, which would have also precluded his departure to Atlanta. Logic suggests that the Ravens should have just promoted Moody knowing they would need him to kick for the rest of the month, maybe longer. Additional reporting from Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic indicated that the Ravens were “willing” to promote Moody to their active roster on Monday. The Falcons, though, offered a better situation after releasing kicker Jason Sanders: a potential long-term job for Moody and a home field enclosed by a dome. It still seems, though, that Baltimore could have headed off this entire issue had they promoted Moody to the active roster last week. It is possible that his agent was keeping tabs on the Falcons’ kicking situation and preferred a practice squad stay to preserve his options. However, Loop has not exactly inspired much confidence that he can deliver key kicks for a team that will need to win at the margins to make the playoffs this year. There is an argument that the Ravens should have identified Moody as their kicker for the foreseeable future and adjusted their roster accordingly. Instead, they will have to scour the NFL’s practice squads and free-agent pool to find their next kicker. Signing Nick Folk, who the Falcons cut to add Moody, would be an ironic twist. After three straight years of leading the league with a field goal conversion rate of 95.5% or better, the 42-year-old’s numbers have collapsed in 2026. He made just 72.2% of his field goals to start the season with two misses inside of 50 yards and a one-for-four mark from beyond.

teamStories.title: Vikings reunite with QB Kirk Cousins, send 3rd-round pick to Raiders
teamStories.summary: Vikings are trading for quarterback Kirk Cousins, sending a 2027 third-round pick to the Raiders.
teamStories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- The Vikings reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins in a trade with the Raiders on Tuesday, sending a 2027 third-round pick to Las Vegas. With the trade, 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' starting quarterback, beginning this week at home against the Seattle Seahawks . Aidan O'Connell will be Mendoza's backup. Cousins posted a goodbye to the Raiders on his Instagram story, writing, "Thank you Raiders Nation! Go get em @fernandomendoza." Trade talks between the teams didn't materialize until Tuesday, according to Las Vegas general manager John Spytek, who said the team was not actively looking to trade Cousins. Spytek said he received a few phone calls about Cousins until the most important one came from Vikings GM Nolan Teasley. He and Teasley spoke on the phone for a while to hammer down the framework on a deal that made sense for both sides. Spytek said he did not speak to Cousins before Tuesday about the possibility of him being traded. "There was nothing to speak about," Spytek said. "We didn't have any expectation that this was coming." Once a trade appeared to be a reality, Spytek and coach Klint Kubiak sat down with Cousins to present the offer they had and why they felt it was the best decision for the Raiders. According to Spytek, "It wasn't the easiest conversation," but it was a very productive one. "We [were] all staring the future in the face here with Fernando, and Kirk's been very open with that, was very open with that when we got him," Spytek said. "We had to decide: Do we want to go forward here over the last eight games, or do we want to take what Minnesota is offering right now? Ultimately, we decided to do that." Unless the Vikings work out a change to Cousins' contract, they will owe him the remainder of his $1.3 million base salary this season and then a $10 million roster bonus this spring. The Vikings released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday to create a spot on the 53-man roster for Cousins. Beckham will re-sign to the team's practice squad, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Vikings have lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start, with their offense managing only 19 points over that stretch. But their defense and special teams rank among the NFL's best, and team decision-makers were determined to optimize their chances at a playoff run. Cousins played for the Vikings from 2018 to 2023, and the Vikings have been unable to find a permanent replacement since his departure to the Atlanta Falcons via free agency in spring 2024. The deal comes less than 24 hours after veteran Carson Wentz turned in the worst performance by a Vikings quarterback since 2006 , compiling a 2.3 QBR while completing 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards and committing three turnovers. Wentz was playing for presumed starter Kyler Murray , who sat out Monday night's game because of a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Murray, who signed a one-year contract with the Vikings this spring, has struggled in his own right and ranks No. 27 in QBR (45.7). Cousins, 38, played two seasons for Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell in Minnesota (2022-23) and was a Pro Bowl selection in 2022 when he threw for 4,547 yards with 29 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. In 2023, he started eight games before suffering a torn Achilles in a game against the Green Bay Packers . Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson enjoyed his finest season in 2022 while playing with Cousins, setting career bests with 128 catches and 1,809 yards, which both led the NFL. He also had eight touchdown catches and led the NFL with 106.4 receiving yards per game. Cousins has rebounded from two years of struggles brought on by his recovery from a torn Achilles to throw 20 touchdown passes this season for the Raiders, second most in the NFL. The team's handling of the position since Cousins' departure contributed heavily to the firing of former general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah in January, and it is threatening to swamp O'Connell and Teasley. The Vikings have had eight quarterbacks start a game since then, and this week would mark the 15th time their starter has changed from one week of a season to another if Wentz does not play against the Packers. At one point in the 2024 season, the Vikings had three former first-round draft picks on their roster: Sam Darnold , J.J. McCarthy and Daniel Jones . But Darnold and Jones both departed as free agents after the season, believing the Vikings would soon commit to McCarthy, but the Vikings gave up on McCarthy this summer after only 10 starts and 253 career pass attempts. Darnold helped the Seahawks to victory in Super Bowl LX last season. Jones was in the MVP conversation with the Indianapolis Colts before tearing his right Achilles tendon last season, and McCarthy has led the New York Giants to wins in his first two starts since the Vikings traded him for a fifth-round pick in September. Since the start of the 2025 season, the Vikings have the NFL's second-worst team QBR (36.3). Cousins was a placeholder at starting quarterback for the Raiders until Mendoza was ready. The Raiders selected Mendoza with the hope that he can become their franchise quarterback, adding stability at the position for the foreseeable future. He showcased the potential to fill that role during his lone season at Indiana. But the Raiders understood they had to be patient with Mendoza's adjustment to the next level. That's why Cousins was named the starting quarterback to begin training camp. He exceeded expectations, throwing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine starts. He completed 64.1% of his passes and finished with a 98 passer rating. ESPN's Ryan McFadden contributed to this report.
