teamStories.title: 2026 NFL trade deadline winners, losers: Kirk Cousins, Josh Downs, Bengals, more
teamStories.summary: Which teams made the best -- and worst -- moves before the NFL trade deadline? We're making sense of all the action.
teamStories.detailText: The NFL trade deadline has come and gone. I will forever remember it as the trade deadline in which the Bengals nearly accidentally traded a third-round pick for Arnold Ebiketie (more on that below). Identifying winners and losers on deadline day is always tough. The Titans, Howie Roseman and Josh Downs will be made winners and losers for their efforts not by my words but by the picks they make or games they win over the next two or three years. Of course, we can grade the quality of their work now (spoiler, they are winners) -- but this isn't the real test. The real test is what comes next . I have six winners and four losers from this year's trade deadline ranging from players to GMs. Let's dive in. Jump to: Cousins | Jefferson | Bengals Downs | Roseman | Taylor | Poles Titans | Chargers | Cardinals Deadline winner: QB Kirk Cousins Cousins is about to have a quarterbacking season for the ages. No, he won't set the passing touchdown record or anything. But let's trace the arc here. Cousins started nine games for a 4-5 Raiders team that was waiting to turn the page to 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza . The entire time he started, he comported himself with the exact attitude and perspective you'd hope to see from a veteran bridge starter. "If I'm not the best option, then I don't want to be out there," Cousins said in late October after the Raiders' fourth straight loss. "The organization will do what they feel is best, but I feel that Fernando's done a great job and has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can to help us win and give him a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually." A beautiful quote. And it echoes what Cousins has said from the beginning: He was in Las Vegas to help the team win but to also give Mendoza an example of how to prepare, speak, compete and perform as an NFL quarterback. If Mendoza looks competent at any part of the 2026 season (and even beyond), Cousins will receive the share of credit due an angel investor. Even if Mendoza was always destined to play well -- he's the first pick, for crying out loud -- Cousins and the Raiders' patient approach with the rookie will be lauded as a contributing factor. So, Cousins has that going for him. His arc continues to Minnesota where the power of friendship welcomes him with open arms. Cousins was a Viking from 2018 to 2023, the last two seasons of which were spent under head coach Kevin O'Connell. The Vikings went 13-4 in 2022 with Cousins before he tore an Achilles midway through the 2023 season. O'Connell's offense isn't just good for Cousins, it's almost built in his image. O'Connell was the quarterbacks coach with Washington in 2017, Cousins' final season on the team. As O'Connell's path split from Cousins, then reunited with him in Minnesota, it has become increasingly clear how much O'Connell's passing game needs a fearless pocket quarterback with the processing speed necessary to handle all the various route adjustments -- not to mention the velocity to hit intermediate throws. Those features have always been the strength of Cousins' game. Cousins isn't just reuniting with pals, though. He's joining a 6-2 Vikings team powered by the league's best and most unique defense. The bar for Cousins -- who is 38 years old and doesn't have as big of an arm as he used to -- has simply never been lower. Carson Wentz's Monday night performance against the Bills dropped it to the floor. As long as Cousins can keep the offense on schedule and manage the time-of-possession battle, Minnesota's defense can win multiple playoff games. It's that dangerous of a group. What else? He gets to throw to Justin Jefferson . That's sick (see below). Cousins could become the first quarterback to start 18 games (the Vikings have had their bye and the Raiders haven't), so he might indeed get to set a record after all. What a season it'll be for Kirk Cousins. Deadline winner: WR Justin Jefferson Is there any individual happier than the Vikings' star receiver right now? No more barely contained frustration on the sideline while cameras follow his every facial expression. A competent quarterback returns to Minnesota -- one who speaks to this day about how throwing the ball near Jefferson is a path to success. Since the start of the 2022 season, Jefferson has averaged 2.73 yards per route run on a 27% target rate when Cousins throws him the football. He has a catch rate of 70% and averages 103.5 yards per game. This season, he was at 2.16 yards per route run at a 30% target share -- the efficiency was way, way down -- with 56.1 yards per game. Almost half as much raw production. He's about to go nuclear with Cousins under center. You can bet the house on that. Deadline loser: Bengals If you have no idea what happened with the Arnold Ebiketie trade and the compensatory pick formula Tuesday morning, don't worry. You've come to the right place. Ebiketie is a veteran edge rusher whom the Eagles signed to a one-year deal worth up to $7.3 million in free agency this past summer. Ebiketie was a regular free agent (i.e., not a player released or cut but whose contract expired with his old team), so he matters in the league's compensatory pick formula. Compensatory picks are additional picks awarded to teams at the end of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh round of the draft, and they are exactly what they sound like: compensation. When a team loses more qualifying free agents than it signs in a given offseason, it is awarded additional picks based on the value of the players it lost. Here's a good example. The Packers lost the following players in free agency in the offseason: Malik Willis (who signed a deal worth $22.5 million in average value with the Dolphins), Quay Walker ($13.5 million), Romeo Doubs ($17 million), Kingsley Enagbare ($9 million) and tackle Rasheed Walker ($4 million). The OverTheCap compensatory pick selections, which are run by a guy named Nick Korte (remember the name!), projected those losses to be worth a third, a fifth, a fifth, a sixth and a seventh, respectively. The Packers signed only one qualifying compensatory free agent on the other side of that scale: cornerback Benjamin St. Juste for $5 million. St. Juste cancels out one of the Packers' incoming compensatory picks -- in this case, it'll be Walker and the seventh, as that's the pick with the most similar value to St. Juste. Now that we understand how compensatory picks work, let's take a look at the Bengals. They lost three free agents in Trey Hendrickson , Joseph Ossai and Noah Fant . They signed two in Bryan Cook and Boye Mafe . But when they tried to trade for Ebiketie , they were acquiring a third player who would have counted against them in the compensatory pick formula. He would have canceled out their one outstanding comp pick, most likely the third-rounder they were in line to receive thanks to Hendrickson's departure. We know this because Korte posted it to social media shortly after the Bengals' trade for Ebiketie was announced. And then, shortly after Korte's post ... it was reported that the Bengals were backing out of the Ebiketie trade. There are a few things to say here. The first is that, had the trade gone through, the Bengals would still have been listed as losers because they lost a third-round pick acquiring a depth edge rusher. That was the worst-case outcome for Cincinnati, and the team successfully avoided it. The second is, even as the Bengals successfully avoided disaster, it is extremely embarrassing to have disaster avoided by a social media post from a cap analyst. The compensatory pick formula is notoriously weird and tricky, but teams have been manipulating it for years now. Multiple teams told me they have in-house software to test moves before they make them to ensure they aren't hurting themselves in the comp pick process. The Bengals either don't have these processes or had a mistake in their process, and their lack of preparedness was caught in glaring light. This was an easily avoidable and needless trip over their own shoelaces. The third is that Zac Taylor was Monday asked about making moves before the trade deadline and said the Bengals would do "nothing ... we're good." And after it's all said and done, he was right! Deadline winner: WR Josh Downs Can you imagine the feeling of getting out of Indianapolis and arriving in Kansas City? Like getting home after a long road trip. Like seeing your high school friends for the first time since you all left for college. Or, perhaps, like Vince Carter the moment his jersey was retired by the Toronto Raptors. If you don't believe me, hear it from the man himself . Downs wins the award for best environmental improvement at the 2026 deadline, as he goes from an offense 31st in EPA per dropback and 32nd in explosive pass rate to an offense that ranks eighth in EPA per dropback and seventh in explosive pass rate. Downs is largely innocent in the investigation of what went wrong with the Colts' passing attack: the injury to receiver Alec Pierce and the play of quarterback Daniel Jones have been the biggest culprits. In Kansas City, Downs will be worryingly as integral to the passing game as he was in Indianapolis, as both teams sorely lack wide receiver depth. But Mahomes is so much more capable a passer than Jones, and the stylistic fit is much better as well: No team throws more screens and quick passes than the Chiefs, which will serve Downs' separation ability from the slot well. Downs doesn't just join a contender with the potential to save its offense and hold the Lombardi Trophy. He's in a contract year, and with the Chiefs' passing attack full of available targets, he could put up career numbers down the stretch. Downs can make millions in 2027 free agency should he produce as the Chiefs need him to. Had Downs become a Steeler, that path to sudden richness would have been narrower. I personally don't think Downs has enough talent as a downfield or contested catch receiver to reach the billing the Chiefs need him to. But it's worth the swing for only an exchange of Day 3 picks. Deadline winner: Howie Roseman When the Eagles got a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-round pick for defensive tackle Jordan Davis , the collective groaning sound you heard immediately afterward was the NFL media machine at large repeating one familiar phrase: Howie season. The Eagles' general manager is known for winning trade deals, and he did it again with this one. To get a first- and a second-round pick for Davis, who has been an early-down run stuffer without much pass rush value to this point in his career, is astonishing work. At last season's trade deadline, Quinnen Williams returned first- and second-round picks as well -- arguably a better first, in that it was the better of the Cowboys' and Packers' 2027 picks. Before this season's deadline, Jeffery Simmons returned the Titans' two first-round picks. Simmons leads all defensive tackles in sacks (six), and Williams is tied for third (five). Davis is tied for 35th with 1.5. Davis was extended in March by the Eagles after a career-best 2025 season in which he was fourth among defensive tackles in run stop rate and run stop EPA. In the Vic Fangio defense, he made light boxes work on early downs, then got off the field for better pass rushers (such as Moro Ojomo , whom the Eagles can now extend) on later downs. In that he was in better shape and playing faster, Davis had 56 third-down pass-rush snaps in 2025 -- more than he'd seen in his first three seasons combined. The Eagles gave him a large extension -- three years, $78 million -- in anticipation of him filling a big role down the stretch. Because Roseman signs early extensions (Davis still had a fifth-year option to play on) and uses future bonuses as built-in restructures, the Eagles were able to suddenly shift gears and trade Davis on the extension instead of keeping him on the books. Had they not gotten that extension done, Davis would have been in a contract year and the Eagles never would have gotten as much trade capital back from the Jaguars. This is the advantage of having a long-term-thinking general manager who has unprecedented job security -- he can value 2029 draft picks and use future money to make optimal decisions now. This was another day on a long list of days that Roseman has won. I'd love to have a clever zag take about why his reputation is bigger than his results, but it isn't. He has the longest view in the room and knows how to pivot off old moves fast. Roseman won the day. It could have been even better if the Ebiketie trade to the Bengals went through -- not because the Eagles would have gotten any more picks out of it but simply because it would have been pretty funny. Deadline winner: Ryan Poles It's important to evaluate trades in a vacuum, and two firsts for Simmons was a steep price no matter which way you slice it. But it does bear saying: That trade looks so much less expensive when you see the price the Jaguars paid for Davis, a player who simply (1) does not play as many snaps as Simmons, (2) does not play as many high-value snaps as Simmons does, (3) is not as productive as Simmons on the snaps that they play and (4) has not produced as consistently as Simmons has. The Bears' GM moved all-in for a defensive tackle just like James Gladstone and the Jaguars did. The playoffs will decide how history views these trades. But the Bears sure got a lot of cover this week, and that's never a bad thing. Deadline loser: RB Jonathan Taylor I feel bad for Taylor. The Colts reportedly got offers centered on a second-round pick and with additional capital behind -- that's a fair price for Taylor -- and they passed on those deals in the hope of bigger returns. Angling for a Christian McCaffrey -esque package -- that's a second, a third and a fourth -- was a reasonable negotiating tactic but never should have been the bar to clear. McCaffrey has a much, much bigger impact on the passing game than Taylor does. McCaffrey was 26 years old when the Panthers traded him to the 49ers in 2022 and had 1,059 touches over 4½ seasons. Taylor turns 28 in January and has 1,925 touches over his seven seasons. The age cliff is likely coming for him soon. Now Taylor is stuck on a Colts offense that will look a lot like the offense he endured in the winter last season: so totally incapable of throwing the football that he will have no room to run. The contenders he could have joined -- the Broncos, Packers, Vikings or Bengals -- all have legitimate runs to the Super Bowl. Taylor could have been the final piece to the puzzle in all of those spots. Given just how talented he is as a big-play runner, I would have believed it, too. The Colts are in for a long and brutal rebuild in that they're missing their 2027 first-round pick because of the Sauce Gardner trade. Taylor might not be in Indianapolis for all of it, but he is for at least the next seven months. He's a fun player stuck in a bad spot. Deadline winner: Titans The Titans are filling the coffers, and rightfully so. After sending Simmons to the Bears for two first-round picks, general manager Mike Borgonzi kept the train rolling by sending Amani Hooker to the Bills for a second-round pick. The Titans now have four top-64 picks in the 2027 draft. That level of flexibility will be huge for them as they determine what to do at quarterback. Second-year passer Cam Ward played the best ball of his NFL career when last we saw him -- a Week 8 late-game loss to the Bengals -- but he'll need to stack several of those days to prove he has turned a corner and deserves to enter Year 3 unchallenged as the Titans' starting quarterback. If there's any uncertainty around Ward, the one-win Titans will evaluate the QB draft landscape (and maybe even the QB trade market, with that extra first in 2028 as additional ammunition). They aren't certain to move on from Ward, but they'll have the resources necessary to move around in the draft if they'd like to. Of course, it is worth noting that the two best Titans defenders are no longer Titans defenders. Hooker doesn't have the same name recognition that Simmons does, but he's an impactful center-fielding safety with range and ball skills, and he has enough size and stopping power to play down in the box. Tennessee has some exciting young players on defense ( Anthony Hill Jr . and Kevin Winston Jr .) to grow with, but it's always sad to see homegrown talent get out of the building without much hardware to show for it. Hooker and Simmons were classmates of the 2019 draft (alongside receiver A.J. Brown ) and went to three straight postseasons under coach Mike Vrabel but never saw a Super Bowl. These trades are wins for the future but reminders of the failures of the past as well. Deadline loser: Chargers I was fully prepared to name the Chargers a loser of the 2026 deadline if they moved no players, as the reporting expected. The ice thawed late Tuesday as they considered dealing some of their expiring contracts: Khalil Mack , Tuli Tuipulotu , Dalvin Tomlinson , Donte Jackson ... and maybe Daiyan Henley . On that list of players, I would have had two functionally untouchable players: Tuipulotu and Henley. Yet, the Chargers sent Henley to the divisional rival Broncos (!) for two Day 3 picks. Of all the trades to make, the Chargers made this one. Henley hit as a third-round pick thanks in large part to the undersized linebacker's success in coverage. Since the start of 2024, when he became a full-time starter, Henley has been targeted 175 times (third among all linebackers), per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has given up two touchdowns to four interceptions with 15 total passes defensed. He has surrendered a passer rating of 82.9 (fourth lowest) and only 6.3 yards per target (11th lowest). His recent play has been more inconsistent than in years past, and there are tackling limitations in the box with a player of his size. But he is a good coverage linebacker in a passing league. I can only imagine the Chargers anticipated not paying Henley in free agency, as he has only one year left on his deal, and traded him for picks while they still could. The Broncos are thrilled by this -- coverage linebacker has been a huge issue for them going back to last season, and a divisional opponent just gave them one for Day 3 capital. I just cannot get my head around the idea that the 0-8 Chargers would make no major moves at this deadline despite the clear need for a total teardown and rebuild ... but then pivot to trading a productive young linebacker for minimal capital. Now they'll continue to run Mack and Jackson and other tradable players for the rest of the season ... and likely get precious little from their departures in 2027 free agency. Poor team-building. Deadline loser: Cardinals There were a few squads that looked like potential big traders as we approached the deadline. The Titans were certainly one, and though they didn't move Tony Pollard or Calvin Ridley , they got some deals done. The Chargers, whom I called losers above, at least made one deal with Daiyan Henley to the Broncos. The Colts could have made bigger splashes with Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor , but they made four deals over the past month, so that's fine. The Arizona Cardinals dealt Marvin Harrison Jr . a month ago, which should not go unremembered. They found a deal for Jacoby Brissett when the Ravens were desperate for a bridge quarterback. But other than that, as the deadline ticked down ... they stood pat. This is a silly missed opportunity. The Cardinals are 3-6 and have shown some life this season with big upset wins over the Rams and the Cowboys. I like a lot of what head coach Mike LaFleur has delivered on offense. Defensively they remain a poor unit across the board -- 32nd in EPA per play, 30th in points per drive allowed -- but at least the offense has kept them in some fights. Yet the offense is broken now. Michael Wilson is on season-ending injured reserve with a neck injury, and QB2-become-QB1 Gardner Minshew II is likely to follow him with a UCL injury in his throwing arm . The Cardinals are down two starting offensive linemen, three starting receivers, both veteran quarterbacks and rookie third overall pick Jeremiyah Love on their Week 1 offensive depth chart. Why, in a market of preposterous safety interest -- both Jessie Bates III and Amani Hooker garnered second-round picks via trade this week -- would you continue to hold on to Budda Baker ? Why, in a market without great edge rusher options, would you hold the best tradable edge rusher in Josh Sweat ? Not only is the season functionally lost given all the offensive injuries, but the defense has been very poor. A new coordinator might step in for Nick Rallis next offseason. Baker and Sweat are both aging players (30 and 29 years old, respectively) who might not fit as well in the next version of the Cardinals' defense. They also might be beyond their prime by the time the Cardinals next become competitive. So many teams are well-equipped for aggressive rebuilds with multiple early selections. The Jets, the Eagles, the Titans. And here come the Cardinals with one future second thanks to the Harrison deal. Other than that, they have only their own Day 1 and 2 picks for the next three seasons. Missed opportunities this week. Deadline loser: Me ... in bingo I need a ruling from the people. I play deadline bingo every year , and this year, we almost won on two different lines. Another defensive tackle deal (after the Davis trade) would have brought us home vertically, and a reunion between a player and an old coordinator would have taken us home horizontally. When I made that square, I was thinking of the classic " Jaelan Phillips to the Eagles reunites with Vic Fangio" or " Rashid Shaheed to the Seahawks to rejoin Klint Kubiak ." You all know the sort of trade I'm talking about. Explicitly made so a player can follow a coach. I was not thinking about Kirk Cousins reuniting with an entire franchise when he returned to Minnesota for a third-round pick. He's getting a familiar head coach in Kevin O'Connell, a familiar offensive coordinator in Wes Phillips, a familiar cafeteria employee, everything. It's a total return to an organization he left only three years ago. Also of note: Falcons center Ryan Neuzil , traded at the absolute buzzer, follows OL coach and running game coordinator Dwayne Ledford to the Ravens. Not technically an OC but so close! Counts? Doesn't count? I lean no, but maybe I'm being too serious about my own made-up trade deadline bingo game. Reach out to me on socials if you feel strongly about the ruling here either way.

teamStories.summary: Tim Keenan promoted from practice squad
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In an unsurprising move, the Las Vegas Raiders signed rookie defensive lineman Tim Keenan to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. Keenan takes the roster spot left vacant from the Raiders’ trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minensota Vikings for a third-round draft pick in 2027. It was likely Keenan would soon be added to the 53-man roster. He was elevated from the practice squad for the past three games, which is the elevation limit for a season. Keenan was a seventh-round draft pick of the Los Angeles Rams this year out of Alabama. He was waived in September. The Raiders then signed him to their practice squad. Keenan played in all three games he was elevated for and he even started in Week 9 at San Francisco, playing a season high 49 percent of the snaps. He has played in 35 percent of the snaps in his three games. He has a total of seven tackles with four coming against the 49ers. Expect him to continue to be part of the playing rotation for the rest of the season. To replace Keenan on the practice squad, the Raiders signed defensive tackle Chris Williams. He has been in the NFL since 2020 and was part of the Falcons’ and Browns’ programs this year.

NFL trade deadline grades: Deals for Kirk Cousins, Josh Downs, Ryan Neuzil
teamStories.summary: Was getting Cousins a home run for the Vikings? Did the Chiefs make a smart move to pick up Josh Downs?
teamStories.detailText: NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals from the 2026 trade deadline , which passed at 4 p.m. ET Tuesday. When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter. Here are our evaluations for all 18 deals, including three Jaguars trades from Monday, three quarterback moves for teams in need and multiple deals involving at least one first-round pick. Jump to a trade: Neuzil/Vorhees | Downs | Henley Hooker | Cousins | Allen | Davis Godchaux | Cisco | Bates | Brissett Simmons | Buckner | Nelson | Harrison Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy Falcons trade C Neuzil to Ravens for G Vorhees Ravens get: C Ryan Neuzil Falcons get: G Andrew Vorhees , 2028 sixth-round pick Falcons grade: C- Ravens grade: B+ The Ravens traded for their second center of this deadline season, with Neuzil heading to Baltimore for Vorhees and a late-round pick. It is a surprising and, at first glance, somewhat confusing deal. Neuzil is a solid center who ranks in the 57th and 50th percentile in pass block win rate and run block win rate at the position, respectively. He is in the last year of his contract. At first glance, it's a little hard to know each team's plan. Cam Jurgens has been struggling since the Ravens acquired him a little over a month ago. Is Neuzil coming in to start over him? Is one of them moving to guard? Or is this just a pure value play? The Falcons have so much cap space in 2027 that they are likely to be very active in free agency and therefore unlikely to receive compensatory picks for players lost. Did the Falcons know they weren't going to bring back Neuzil and dealt him to avoid losing him for nothing? That's possible, though I would have thought they would have managed more of a return. But maybe that's what attracted the Ravens -- they saw this as a value play that could net them a profit in terms of compensatory picks with upside that Neuzil could help them now and in the future. I don't mind that for Baltimore, especially since the Jurgens deal already is looking like a mistake. But it's a tougher sell for the Falcons. I would much rather try to re-sign Neuzil to a long-term deal (perhaps they did). If they were going to trade Neuzil, was this really the best they could get? And though the Falcons are hardly contenders, this certainly won't help quarterback Michael Penix Jr . down the stretch. Backup Corey Levin will presumably start going forward. Vorhees figures to be a depth guard for the Falcons as he was for the Ravens. Colts trade WR Downs to Chiefs Chiefs get: WR Josh Downs , 2027 seventh-round pick Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick Chiefs grade: B+ Colts grade: B+ Downs is free! The slot receiver is out of Indianapolis and now has a chance to be a major part of the Chiefs' offense down the stretch and, perhaps, during a playoff run. Downs has recorded 354 receiving yards on 33 receptions this season (1.2 yards per route run) but has recorded 1.7 yards per route run over the course of his career. But as any fantasy football diehard will tell you, Downs has much more potential than that. Over his four seasons, Downs has a 68 open score in ESPN's receiver scores , which evaluate a receiver's ability to get open on all routes -- not only the ones when he is targeted. And that 68 score means Downs is well above average. Though this has hardly been a guarantee for past Chiefs receivers, it is possible that playing with Patrick Mahomes will unlock a higher level of production from Downs. Kansas City is back to being a contender -- the Chiefs entered Tuesday with a 96% chance to reach the playoffs and a 7% chance to win the Super Bowl -- but their offense hasn't felt as if it has reached its maximum potential. The Chiefs rank only eighth in EPA per dropback but have been able to outperform that because of the rushing success of Kenneth Walker III . Both Rashee Rice (35%) and Xavier Worthy (20%) spend time in the slot, but I expect those numbers will drop with Downs, who aligned in the slot 51% of the time in Indianapolis this season, now on the team. Over his career, Rice's numbers have been slightly worse in the slot (2.3 yards per route run) compared with when he's lined up outside or elsewhere (2.8). The price here is similar to what the Seahawks gave up last year for Rashid Shaheed who, like Downs, was in a contract year. Perhaps the Chiefs will re-sign Downs as the Seahawks did with Shaheed but if not, they should be in line for a likely compensatory pick given that Kansas City does not have much cap room in 2027. Given the Chiefs' need to augment the offense and status as a true contender, I think this is a worthwhile addition at this price. As for the Colts, while I wouldn't have been opposed to them signing Downs to a long-term deal given his age (25) and talent, dealing him is quite logical. They are in the midst of a teardown and if Downs left via free agency, they would not recoup this much value in a compensatory pick -- if they even got one. Chargers trade LB Henley to Broncos Broncos get: LB Daiyan Henley Chargers get: 2027 fourth-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick Broncos: C+ Chargers: B+ The winless Chargers finally decided to trade a player before the deadline, dealing Henley, in the final year of his contract, to the division-rival Broncos. It's an interesting deal because linebacker did not look like a particular need for Denver. Alex Singleton leads all linebackers in run stop win rate this season and Justin Strnad is a good coverage player. Henley's numbers are OK this season. He ranks in the 46th percentile and has allowed 0.9 yards per coverage snap (average for the position) per NFL Next Gen Stats. I think it's reasonable for Denver to be adding at the deadline, but this is not trivial draft capital to give up for a player who is going to provide depth or be part of a rotation. I'm on board with this move for the Chargers. Though Henley could have been a player they kept around given that he will turn only 27 later this month, he wasn't a difference-maker that they had to hang on to. And if he left in free agency, they would not have recouped this value via a compensatory pick even if they had gotten one -- which was also unlikely given their considerable 2027 cap space. On the other hand, Denver does have a decent change to recoup a compensatory pick if Henley walks, with both Singleton and Strnad signed into 2027 or later (though Singleton will turn 33 next month). Some will criticize the Chargers trading a player within the division, but that is foolish. If anything, the teams the Chargers should most want to take draft capital from ought to be other teams in the AFC West. The only real question for the Chargers: Why didn't they trade more players? Titans trade S Hooker to Bills Bills get: S Amani Hooker , 2027 fifth-round pick Titans get: 2027 second-round pick Bills grade: C+ Titans grade: A- As the Bills push for a title run, safety was an obvious place for an upgrade. I thought the answer might be Jessie Bates III , but the Jaguars -- arguably Buffalo's biggest threat in the AFC -- traded for the former Falcons safety Monday. After the team released C.J. Gardner-Johnson last week, Damar Hamlin was left playing next to Cole Bishop , with Geno Stone as the third safety. In Hooker, the Titans upgrade from Hamlin and pick up a player who has been having an impactful season in Tennessee. Hooker has recorded five interceptions and six passes defensed this season with the Titans, good enough to have the sixth-best EPA allowed on targets among safeties. All current metrics on safeties are quite noisy, but some of the others are not as strong: 1.0 yards per coverage snap both this season and last, and positive EPA allowed in 2025. The Bills will be getting him on a value contract, as they will be on the hook for the rest of Hooker's roughly $8.9 million in salary and per game roster bonuses this year, and then will be slated to pay him a non-guaranteed $10.3 million in 2027 and $13.5 million in 2028, per OverTheCap.com . That's less than Hooker would make on the open market, I believe, though not free. So Hooker is an upgrade at a position of need for a Super Bowl-contending team and will save them a few million per year relative to the market. But is that worth a second-round pick? It strikes me as rich. Hooker is a good player but not a star -- he has never been a Pro Bowl selection or All-Pro and only snuck into Jeremy Fowler's NFL evaluator survey of top safeties in the "also receiving votes" category. As a result, the compensation here is a bit steep. Raiders trade QB Cousins to Vikings Vikings get: QB Kirk Cousins Raiders get: 2027 third-round pick Vikings grade: A Raiders grade: B+ The Vikings were in the unusual position of being Super Bowl contenders that desperately needed a quarterback. And Tuesday was essentially the last day they could get one. Kyler Murray is both hurt and clearly not a fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense. Murray has struggled this season and currently ranks 27th in QBR (45.7). Carson Wentz was abysmal in relief Monday night against the Bills , consistently failing to throw on target while the all-world Vikings defense somehow kept Josh Allen in check in the loss. It's hard to overstate the urgency with which the Vikings needed to upgrade at quarterback. They are 6-2 and had a 65% chance to reach the playoffs prior to this trade, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . Minnesota has a Super Bowl-caliber defense, but that defense is fueled by its coach -- defensive coordinator Brian Flores -- rather than superstar players. Which means their Super Bowl window will evaporate into thin air the moment Flores leaves for another job, which could happen as soon as next offseason. The Vikings were not going to reach the Super Bowl with the offense in had in the first eight games. So, the 38-year-old Cousins was a perfect player to target. He has familiarity and past success in O'Connell's system, and the presence of first overall pick Fernando Mendoza made it logical for the Raiders to deal Cousins before the deadline. And, perhaps most importantly, he's been playing very well! Cousins ranks 12th in QBR (62.8) this season on a team that has star tight end Brock Bowers but is lacking at wide receiver. Cousins has a 13.5% off-target rate (eighth best), a plus-4.0% completion percentage over expected (sixth best) and a 3.4% sack rate (second best). The last time Cousins was in Minnesota was in 2023, when he was playing some of the best football of his career before suffering a season-ending Achilles tear . His 64.0 QBR was the seventh best in the league through eight games. His 11% off-target rate that season and plus-4.6% completion percentage over expected ranked first and second in the league, respectively. Cousins left as a free agent to sign with the Falcons , where he recorded a 48.5 QBR over 24 games spanning two seasons. He then signed as a bridge quarterback with the Raiders. But Cousins played well enough to keep the job until Tuesday's deadline. His addition changes Minnesota's trajectory and brings it back into the group of viable Super Bowl contenders. For the Vikings to rescue their season in exchange for a third-round pick and a $10 million roster bonus that they will have to pay next season is very easily worth it, especially since their window might be super tight. Despite posturing that they might hold Cousins, this was always the best move for the Raiders. Had they not dealt Cousins, he likely would have played a couple more games before they turned the keys over to Mendoza. Was keeping that plan worth a third-round pick and $10 million? Surely not. There's an argument that starting Mendoza's career with games against the Seahawks and Broncos defenses will stunt his development. I don't really buy that, but if the Raiders are concerned they could play Aidan O'Connell for a few weeks and let Mendoza take over after, perhaps following their Week 13 bye. Either way, it made sense for them to get the third-round pick (and save the money). Colts trade WR Allen to 49ers 49ers get: WR Keenan Allen Colts get: 2027 sixth-round pick 49ers grade: B Colts grade: B The 49ers are bringing in reinforcements to help their injury-plagued wide receiver position. With Ricky Pearsall out for the season , De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk on IR, and Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr . each having missed the past couple of games, San Francisco is hurting for pass catchers. Plenty of people connected the 49ers to Colts wide receiver Josh Downs leading up to the trade deadline, but it is actually the 34-year-old Allen who is heading to San Francisco. The Colts signed the 14-year veteran to a one-year, $3.3 million contract when they were hurting at wide receiver with Alec Pierce recovering from ankle surgery . Allen has recorded 40 receptions for 351 yards (1.8 yards per route run) in eight games for the Colts. He has been targeted on 30% of his routes -- a massive number -- while recording a low average depth of target (8.5 yards). Allen recorded open, catch and YAC scores of 39, 66 and 41, respectively in ESPN's player-tracking-based receiver scores -- mediocre numbers when combined together. If I were the 49ers, I would certainly much rather have had Downs. But he also would have cost more draft capital. Despite his age, Allen can be part of the solution to help the 49ers get past their current injury turmoil until help returns. His track record and the numbers that he accumulated in Indianapolis this season suggest he can be useful in the short term. So a sixth-round pick is worth it, especially considering the 49ers' status as a Super Bowl favorite. While Allen is typically thought of as a slot receiver, he doesn't have to exclusively play there. He's only played there on 24% of his snaps this season. Porter reportedly had contract demands up at the top of the cornerback market, where Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez recently reset elite deals to clear $33 million annually. I'm not sold that Porter is a top-tier corner deserving of that top money. But because the Steelers let this go on for so long and bleed into the regular season, they were only able to acquire a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick for a young, ascendent cover corner. They could have -- and should have -- gotten at least a first-round pick by playing this differently and dealing Porter in the spring or earlier in the summer. -- Solak Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick Giants grade: C Vikings grade: B+ A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension , New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks. Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft. McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become Minnesota's starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good. McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for. During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray , but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz , too. That is a telling red flag. So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan. It is difficult to know from the outside which other backup quarterbacks would have been available, but McCarthy still does not seem like an ideal choice. Mac Jones and Spencer Rattler ought to have been the team's first calls (maybe they were). Kirk Cousins probably is off the board with the Raiders sitting at 3-0. Mitchell Trubisky might have been available, considering this already looks like a lost season for Tennessee. And I'm assuming Gardner Minshew II surely must be available, considering he sits in veteran no-man's land between Jacoby Brissett and rookie Carson Beck in Arizona. Stetson Bennett IV could have been an option, too, after the Rams selected Ty Simpson in the first round of this year's draft. I'll grant that some of those options have less upside than McCarthy. But the Giants' front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It's not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn't have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him! Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy's ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn't beat out Wentz. If he wasn't going to be the Vikings' backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not. -- Walder

teamStories.title: Raiders trade deadline notes
teamStories.summary: Las Vegas only decides to part ways with veteran quarterback
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders traded quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings for a 3rd round pick (the Vikings’ second in the round) Tuesday. it opens the door for the Raiders play No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza, who general manager John Spytek confirmed Tuesday afternoon will be the starter moving forward. Here are some notes about their deadline decisions: The Raiders, at 4-5, didn’t decide to make it a fire sale. They also didn’t opt to add at the trade deadline either as they have lost five of the last six games after starting 3-0. NFL reporter Jordan Schulz reported that the Raiders did receive recent trade calls on star defensive end Maxx Crosby, but resisted them after a nixed trade with the Baltimore Ravens in March. Because the Raiders have already agreed to trade Crosby once, expect them to receive more calls in the future, including next offseason. There is no word if the Raiders had any interest in pending free agents, wide receiver Tre Tucker and safety Jeremy Chinn. It will be interesting to see if they try to extend them in the offseason. Spytek said he received calls on multiple players without getting into detail. Despite needs at some posts, including at wide receiver and defensive tackle, the Raiders did not add at the deadline. Spytek said the Cousins’ trade is not an indication the team is giving up on the season. Coach Klint Kubiak said Mendoza is prepared, physically and mentally, for this task and he praised Cousin for his influence on the rookie. Spytek said Mendoza has passed every test since being drafted and he helped the Raiders make the tough decision to deal Cousins. Spytek said Mendoza’s play in practice was difficult to ignore. Spytek said he only received calls on Cousins and did not make any himself. The talks with Minnesota emerged Tuesday morning after Carson Wentz’s horrible showing in a loss Monday night. Spytek said the team did not expect this to happen before Tuesday, thus he had no previous conversations with Cousins about it. Spytek said he and Kubiak spent a lot of time before agreeing to the Cousins trade, but, ultimately decided it was best for the franchise.

teamStories.title: Kirk Cousins Delivers Heartfelt Message to Mendoza After Raiders Trade
Kirk Cousins is returning to Vikings after trade deadline deal with Raiders
Sloppy Raiders blasted by 49ers in return to the Bay Area
What the Kirk Cousins trade means for the Vikings and the Raiders
teamStories.summary: We answered big questions surrounding the trade of quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Raiders to the Vikings.
teamStories.detailText: Kirk Cousins played what appeared to be his final game for the Minnesota Vikings on Oct. 29, 2023. On that afternoon at Lambeau Field, Cousins had thrown for 274 yards and two touchdowns when he tore his right Achilles tendon and was lost for the season. That moment set off a three-year odyssey that improbably ended the way it began. Cousins returned Tuesday to the Vikings, via a trade that sent their 2027 third-round draft pick to the Las Vegas Raiders , and could start Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). Since then, the Vikings have tried eight different starting quarterbacks and made a total of 14 different in-season quarterback changes. The most recent came Monday night at U.S. Bank Stadium, where Carson Wentz -- starting in place of the injured Kyler Murray -- produced the Vikings' worst game by a starting quarterback since 2006. The Vikings have lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start, and their decision-makers did not want to waste what has been an elite-level defense and special teams performance this season with poor quarterback play. In Las Vegas, the door is now wide open for Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 pick of the 2026 NFL draft, to step into his role as the long-term franchise quarterback. ESPN Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert, Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden, national reporter Jeremy Fowler and fantasy's Michael F. Florio take a closer look at the questions and issues involved. What's a realistic expectation for the Vikings' offense with Cousins at QB? The offense under coach Kevin O'Connell has been tough for quarterbacks of all experience levels to master, and Cousins talked often in 2022 about his struggles to feel comfortable in it. But by the middle of the 2023 season, Cousins was playing better than he ever had in a Minnesota uniform. He led the NFL with 18 touchdown passes over eight games and had a 64 QBR. All of which goes to say that if he can pick up where he left off, the Vikings could soon resurrect their dormant passing offense. But it's only natural to expect Cousins to need some time to adjust after three years away, and it also might be a generous assumption that the quarterback position is the only cause of their issues this season. It's only fair to say that playcalling, pass protection and run game efficiency have also contributed. -- Seifert If Cousins isn't able to ignite the Vikings' offense, what does it mean for Kevin O'Connell's future in Minnesota? If that is the outcome, and the Vikings miss the playoffs following a 6-0 start, there won't be many people left to blame. Owners Zygi and Mark Wilf have already fired general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, whom they hired alongside O'Connell in 2022. O'Connell reports directly to the Wilfs, not to new general manager Nolan Teasley, but the Vikings' offensive collapse now goes all the way back to the start of the 2025 season. If he can't make it work with Cousins -- and to be fair it's far from easy to integrate a new starting quarterback in midseason -- then O'Connell's future will at the very least come under heavy offseason scrutiny. The Wilfs love the locker room culture O'Connell has created with his empathetic personality, but his specialty on the field -- offense, in particular the passing game -- has been substandard for an extended period of time. -- Seifert Is Fernando Mendoza now the Raiders' starting quarterback? What should we expect from him? GM John Spytek officially named Mendoza the Raiders' starting quarterback on Tuesday. Despite Mendoza not playing in games, the Raiders have been pleased with the progress that he made behind the scenes. Quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan has praised Mendoza for developing stronger command of the offense. He noticed Mendoza's command and how the game slowed down for him during his debut against the Patriots in Week 5. Sure, Mendoza doesn't have the experience that Cousins possessed (nor does Aidan O'Connell ). But the reigning Heisman Trophy winner has a stronger arm than Cousins. On top of that, Mendoza has better mobility, which will be helpful on bootleg plays. Mendoza will not be perfect and patience will be required, especially in the first few weeks as the starter. It does help that he has the best tight ends room in the league with Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer , and the offensive line has been fairly solid in pass protection. Mendoza taking over will be a perfect time for the Raiders to fix their running game to better support the rookie. -- McFadden What does this trade mean for the fantasy value of players in Minnesota and Las Vegas? The biggest winner of this trade is wide receiver Justin Jefferson . He has averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game this season, after averaging 61.6 per game in 2025. In his four seasons with Cousins, Jefferson averaged 98 yards per game and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. He remains a must-start fantasy option and could once again reach elite status with Cousins, especially since the Vikings have the seventh-best remaining WR schedule. Cousins had been enjoying a resurgence in Vegas this season, averaging 19.1 fantasy points per game and is currently the QB5 in total points. Perhaps there is a ramp-up period as he adjusts to a new team, but Cousins knows O'Connell's system well. Expect Cousins to hold similar fantasy value with the Vikings as he did with the Raiders, in the low-end QB1/high-end QB2 range. As for the Raiders, while Mendoza is very talented, a change to a rookie QB always adds some volatility. He is worth adding off the waiver wire for QB-needy teams, as there will be games when Mendoza has to throw a lot due to the Raiders' defense. Tight end Brock Bowers remains a must-start option and should continue to be the focal point of the Raiders' passing attack. Ashton Jeanty has been trending down, but he still remains in play as an RB2 due to his pass game usage. I anticipate Mendoza will continue to dump the ball off at a high rate. As for the Raiders' secondary fantasy options -- WR Tre Tucker and TE Michael Mayer -- it is best to get away from them for the time being. Perhaps Mendoza can keep all these options afloat like Cousins did, but those are high expectations for a rookie. -- Florio Did the Vikings explore other options, or was it all Cousins? The Vikings did explore their options, but they had a pretty good feeling all roads would lead them to Cousins. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones was in the mix, but sources believed he was more of a backup option to Cousins. Minnesota was linked to New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith , even if through a basic inquiry. The Jets had no interest in moving on from Smith, who was on the Vikings' radar back in March. It's possible the Vikings made other calls as they scanned the quarterback landscape, but acquiring Cousins, given his history in Minnesota and the reasonable price tag, always made the most sense. -- Fowler How well-liked does Cousins remain in the Vikings' building after leaving three years ago? On a personal level, Cousins was loved within the Vikings' practice building by the end of his tenure. He had a much better personal relationship with O'Connell than he did with former coach Mike Zimmer, and teammates gleefully helped create the "Kirko Chains" alter ego by egging on Cousins to take off his shirt and wear jewelry on team flights. When he returned to U.S. Bank Stadium in 2024 as a member of the Atlanta Falcons , a long line of well-wishers waited in a makeshift receiving line to embrace him after the game. On the field, the Vikings were willing to let Cousins move on in free agency because they hoped to elevate the position in a way that could help them compete better in the playoffs. What they found, however, is that the grass is not always greener on the other side. -- Seifert What does this trade mean for Las Vegas' playoff hopes -- and Minnesota's NFC North chances? Raiders: Yes, the Raiders are still in the hunt. But the roster has too many flaws to keep it up. They have been one of the worst defenses in the league, allowing 30-plus in six straight weeks, while they have struggled running the ball. Even if Cousins stayed, it would've been challenging to stay in the playoff mix, especially with upcoming matchups against Seattle and Denver. Still, Mendoza is given an opportunity to keep the Raiders in the postseason discussion despite it seeming like a tall task. Las Vegas' schedule after its Week 13 bye is favorable (Chargers, Broncos, Titans, Cardinals, Chiefs), meaning it could be in position for a late-season run at a wild-card spot if it can pull off one to two wins in the next three weeks. However, the Raiders understood the reality of their situation from the beginning. Their goal is to make a serious postseason push in 2027 and beyond. -- McFadden Vikings: This trade is best viewed as a way to keep the Vikings in the fight in the NFC North, the NFL's deepest division. Cousins at 38 is no miracle worker, and the Vikings (6-2) face a daunting schedule against the Packers (6-3) and then the San Francisco 49ers (7-1) next week in Mexico City. But without competitive quarterback play, which they were not getting from Wentz or Murray, they were in position to collapse from their 6-0 start. Their chances of at least making the playoffs appear substantially higher. -- Seifert

headlines.title: Warriors' Will Richard out indefinitely
headlines.summary: The Warriors say guard Will Richard is out indefinitely with a torn UCL in his left thumb. Richard had been giving the team key minutes as both a starter and a reserve. Golden State has won seven straight games since an 0–3 start, and Richard's role has been part of that run.

headlines.title: Grizzlies still perfect on the road
headlines.summary: Memphis beat the short-handed Raptors 118–102 in Toronto, improving to 5-0 on the road. Ty Jerome scored 27 points and Cameron Boozer added 22 points, eight rebounds and eight assists. The Grizzlies are the only NBA team without a road loss this season. Toronto was missing Kawhi Leonard, Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley.

headlines.title: Hornets end losing streak with a rout of the Cavs
headlines.summary: Charlotte beat Cleveland 124–112 to snap a six-game losing streak. Grayson Allen scored 27 points and Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds. The Cavaliers trailed by as many as 33 points against the league's worst offence. Cleveland is 5-6 and seventh in the East, and it plays at the Knicks on national TV on Wednesday.

headlines.title: Doc Rivers apologises to Giannis
headlines.summary: Doc Rivers says he reached out to Giannis Antetokounmpo to apologise for questioning his basketball IQ. Rivers says he meant that the force Antetokounmpo plays with can get in the way of his feel.

headlines.title: Thunder land Nique Clifford from Kings for two second-rounders
headlines.summary: Oklahoma City has traded for wing Nique Clifford from Sacramento. The Kings receive a 2028 Utah second-round pick and a 2030 Minnesota second-round pick. The Thunder have lost starters Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for several months, perhaps the rest of the season, so they went looking for wing depth. Clifford, the No. 24 pick in 2025, had fallen out of Sacramento's rotation, averaging 6.3 minutes and 1.6 points. He makes $3.3 million this season. The Thunder are reportedly likely to waive Dalen Terry to make room.

headlines.title: Dončić out with lower back tightness
headlines.summary: Luka Dončić has been ruled out of the Lakers' game against Detroit with lower back tightness, and the Lakers start a four-game road trip without him. He was listed as questionable on Saturday, a day after scoring a season-high 53 points against Portland. Over nine games he is averaging 40.1 points, 7.8 rebounds and 7.7 assists. This is the second game he has missed with back tightness. Detroit, at 6–2, has given up the fewest points per game in the league.

headlines.title: Jalen Duren out at least two more weeks with hamstring strain
headlines.summary: Pistons centre Jalen Duren is out at least two more weeks with a strained right hamstring. He has been sidelined since Detroit's game against Miami on 23 October. Duren has started on-court activities, and the Pistons will update his status again in two weeks. Detroit plays six of its next nine games on the road.

headlines.title: Dončić scores 53 as the Lakers beat Portland
headlines.summary: Luka Dončić had 53 points, five rebounds, five assists and five three-pointers in the Lakers’ 124–118 win over the Trail Blazers. Austin Reaves added 25 points and four steals. Portland’s Deni Avdija had 22 points, nine rebounds and 11 assists, and Damian Lillard scored 22, but the Blazers fell to 6–2. Dončić is averaging 40.1 points per game, the best in the league.

headlines.title: Jaguars go all in before the deadline
headlines.summary: Jacksonville traded a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for Davis. The same day, the Jaguars sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Falcons for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, and sent defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to the Saints for a 2028 sixth-round pick. Eagles reports suggest the Davis deal may also tie into a defensive coordinator change, with Jim Schwartz mentioned as a possible replacement if Vic Fangio retires.

headlines.title: Colts open to trading Jonathan Taylor
headlines.summary: The Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor, and several teams are reportedly interested. The Vikings, Broncos and Packers are named as possible landing spots as the deadline approaches. Indianapolis is in a rough spot and has lost five straight games.

headlines.title: Cardinals lose Gardner Minshew and Michael Wilson
headlines.summary: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew probably needs season-ending surgery on his right UCL, according to ESPN sources. Top receiver Michael Wilson is also out for the season with a neck fracture. Arizona has signed veteran quarterback Josh Johnson off the Bengals practice squad.

headlines.title: Patriots' Stevenson hurt in blowout loss
headlines.summary: Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson has a knee tendon issue that is not expected to need surgery. He was hurt late in the third quarter of the loss to the Packers, when New England trailed 42–14. Stevenson has played 65% of the offensive snaps, with 399 yards on 102 carries and two touchdowns. The Patriots' next game is against the Lions in Munich, and they have a bye after it.

headlines.title: Chiefs bounce back with 35–12 win over Jets
headlines.summary: Kansas City beat the Jets 35–12 to end a two-game losing streak, after losses to the Seahawks and Broncos. Kenneth Walker scored three touchdowns, two of them receiving from Patrick Mahomes, and ran for 102 yards. Mahomes threw for 242 yards. Kansas City led 14–12 at halftime, then scored twice in the third quarter, when the Jets were credited with minus-9 yards. The Chiefs sacked Geno Smith five times, and New York's star receiver Garrett Wilson missed the game with a concussion.

headlines.title: Garrett's three sacks help Rams beat Commanders 20–13
headlines.summary: Los Angeles beat Washington 20–13 for its third straight win. Myles Garrett had three sacks, and Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Stafford threw for 228 yards and a touchdown, with one interception. Blake Corum scored on the ground. Jayden Daniels threw for 274 yards for Washington, which fell to 2–5–1.

headlines.title: Giants beat Eagles 19–11 with McCarthy back
headlines.summary: The Giants beat the Eagles 19–11 in an NFC East game decided by one score. J.J. McCarthy returned after a hip injury had sent him to the locker room, with Jameis Winston briefly coming in for him. McCarthy completed 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards. Arvell Reese had three sacks and 12 tackles. Joe Milton threw for 169 yards for the Eagles, who fell to 2–7.

headlines.title: Burrow throws three touchdowns as Bengals beat Falcons 34–17
headlines.summary: Joe Burrow threw for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and Ja'Marr Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a score. Cincinnati won 34–17 in Atlanta. Chase Brown ran for 57 yards. Michael Penix Jr. threw for 162 yards with a touchdown and an interception for the Falcons, and Bijan Robinson ran for 100 yards and a touchdown in the loss. Barrett Carter had an interception for Cincinnati.
